contraindications_zh: 溫病初起、表有鬱熱而見發熱口渴、脈數者不宜 —— 辛溫助熱。
表實無汗者禁用 —— 此為麻黃湯證，誤用桂枝湯則邪無出路。《傷寒論》：「桂枝本為解肌，若其人脈浮緊、發熱汗不出者，不可與之也。」
酒客（濕熱內蘊者）不宜，服之易致嘔。
暑天或天候炎熱時宜謹慎使用。
contraindications_en: Contraindicated for those with Exterior Cold with Interior Heat.
Contraindicated for those with Tai Yang Shang Han.
Contraindicated for those who drink alcohol frequently.
Use caution during the summer or spells of hot weather.

contraindications_zh: 表實無汗者禁用 —— 此為麻黃湯證，誤用桂枝湯則邪無出路。《傷寒論》：「桂枝本為解肌，若其人脈浮緊、發熱汗不出者，不可與之也。」
溫病初起、表有鬱熱而見發熱口渴、脈數者不宜 —— 辛溫助熱。
酒客（濕熱內蘊者）不宜，服之易致嘔。
表寒裡熱者禁用。
夏季或天氣炎熱時慎用。
contraindications_en: Contraindicated for those with Tai Yang Shang Han.
Not appropriate for early-stage warm disease with constrained heat in the exterior, presenting with fever, thirst, and a rapid pulse — acrid-warm herbs would assist the heat.
Contraindicated for those who drink alcohol frequently.
Contraindicated for those with Exterior Cold with Interior Heat.
Use caution during the summer or spells of hot weather.

modifications_zh: 頭痛 → 加羌活、白芷、川芎、蔓荊子
咳嗽痰多 → 加紫蘇子、半夏
modifications_en: Headaches → add Qiang Huo, Bai Zhi, Chuan Xiong and Man Jing Zi
Coughing with copious sputum → add Zi Su Zi and Ban Xia

modifications_zh: 頭痛：分別加羌活、白芷、川芎、蔓荊子，以分別引藥入各經。
咳嗽痰多：加紫蘇子、半夏，以增強燥濕與降氣之效。
modifications_en: For headaches, add Qiang Huo, Bai Zhi, Chuan Xiong, or Man Jing Zi respectively, to guide the effect into each meridian.
For coughing with copious sputum, add Zi Su Zi and Ban Xia, for a stronger damp-drying and qi-downward-moving effect.

actions_en: Induces sweating and releases the Exterior
Raises fluids and relaxes the sinews

modifications_en: Without cough and sputum → remove Jie Geng and Qian Hu

modifications_zh: 無咳嗽咳痰者：減桔梗、前胡。
急性風濕熱：加桂枝、知母、忍冬藤、桑枝。
風濕痺痛：減桔梗、前胡，加威靈仙、秦艽、烏頭。
風毒癮疹瘙癢：加蟬蛻、苦參。
無濕象者：減羌活、獨活、茯苓。
modifications_en: When there is no presentation of cough and sputum, remove Jie Geng and Qian Hu.
For acute rheumatic fever, add Gui Zhi, Zhi Mu, Ren Dong Teng, and Sang Zhi.
For pains due to wind-damp Bi, remove Jie Geng and Qian Hu, and add Wei Ling Xian, Qin Jiao, and Wu Tou.
For wind toxic rashes with itchiness, add Chan Tui and Ku Shen.
When there is no damp presentation, remove Qiang Huo, Du Huo, and Fu Ling.

modifications_zh: 氣分火盛 → 加石膏、知母，或大青葉、板藍根
陰虛見脈細數 → 去黃連
營分熱盛 → 重用水牛角、生地、玄參
陰液耗傷甚 → 加沙參
抽搐震顫 → 加鉤藤、地龍
modifications_en: Severe Qi-level fire → add Shi Gao and Zhi Mu, or Da Qing Ye and Ban Lan Gen
Yin deficiency with thready rapid pulse → remove Huang Lian
Severe Ying-level heat → increase Shui Niu Jiao, Sheng Di and Xuan Shen
Severe Yin depletion → add Sha Shen
Tremors and spasms → add Gou Teng and Di Long

modifications_zh: 氣分火熱熾盛：加石膏、知母，或大青葉、板藍根。
陰虛而脈細數：減黃連。
營分熱盛：重用水牛角、生地黃、玄參。
陰液耗傷甚者：加沙參。
抽搐痙攣：加鉤藤、地龍。
modifications_en: For severe qi-level fire, add Shi Gao and Zhi Mu, or Da Qing Ye and Ban Lan Gen.
For yin deficiency with a thready rapid pulse, remove Huang Lian.
For severe ying-level heat, increase the dosage of Shui Niu Jiao, Sheng Di, and Xuan Shen.
For severe yin depletion, add Sha Shen.
For tremors and spasms, add Gou Teng and Di Long.

contraindications_zh: 本方證的病機是正虛邪實，所以一面用苦寒瀉火，一面以酸甘滋陰。如果體內虛多邪少，則非本方所宜！
contraindications_en: The pathomechanism of this pattern is deficiency of the righteous Qi combined with excess pathogenic Heat, so the formula simultaneously drains Fire with bitter-cold herbs and enriches Yin with sour-sweet herbs. If the patient's presentation is predominantly deficient with little excess pathogen, this formula is not appropriate.

contraindications_en: The pattern this formula treats is deficiency of the upright qi with an excess pathogen, so it drains Fire with bitter cold while enriching Yin with sour and sweet. Where deficiency predominates and the pathogen is minor, this formula is not appropriate.

modifications_zh: 血分熱毒甚者：加生地黃、牡丹皮、金銀花。
裡急後重甚者：加木香、檳榔、白芍。
便中膿血多者：加赤芍、牡丹皮、地榆。
兼食積：加焦山楂、枳實。
modifications_en: For severe heat toxin in the blood, add Sheng Di, Dan Pi, and Jin Yin Hua.
For severe tenesmus, add Mu Xiang, Bing Lang, and Bai Shao.
For more pus and blood in the stool, add Chi Shao, Dan Pi, and Di Yu.
With food stagnation, add Jiao (charred) Shan Zha and Zhi Shi.

modifications_zh: 加減：
陰虛血熱者：可加桑葉、首烏、烏梅等藥物，增強滋陰養血之功。
熱入血室，邪結血分：可加歸鬚、新絳、東白薇、銀胡、地骨皮、鮮茅根、來復丹等藥物，加強清熱涼血、活血化瘀之效。
modifications_en: Modifications:
For Yin deficiency with Heat in the Blood: add Sang Ye (Mulberry Leaf), Shou Wu (Fleeceflower Root) and Wu Mei (Mume Fruit) to strengthen the nourishing of Yin and Blood.

For Heat entering the Blood Chamber with the pathogen binding in the Blood aspect: add Dang Gui Xu (Tangkuei Root Tip), Xin Jiang (madder-red preparation), Dong Bai Wei (Baiwei Root), Yin Hu (Silvery Bupleurum), Di Gu Pi (Lycium Root Bark), fresh Bai Mao Gen (Imperata Rhizome) and Lai Fu Dan (a patent pill) to strengthen clearing Heat, cooling the Blood and dispersing Blood stasis.

modifications_zh: 加減：

modifications_en: Modifications:
Yin Deficiency with Blood Heat: add herbs such as Sang Ye, Shou Wu and Wu Mei to strengthen enriching Yin and nourishing Blood.

Heat entering the Blood chamber, pathogen bound in the Blood level: add herbs such as Gui Xu, Xin Jiang, Dong Bai Wei, Yin Hu, Di Gu Pi, fresh Bai Mao Gen and Lai Fu Dan to strengthen clearing Heat, cooling the Blood, moving Blood and transforming stasis.

modifications_zh: 虛火較輕 → 去黃連、黃芩，加知母

盜汗甚 → 加煅龍骨、煅牡蠣、五味子、麻黃根
自汗 → 去黃連、黃芩、黃柏，加黨參、浮小麥、白朮

modifications_en: Mild deficiency fire → remove Huang Lian and Huang Qin; add Zhi Mu
Excess Yang rising with Yin deficiency → add Bai Shao and Gui Ban
Severe night sweats → add Duan Long Gu, Duan Mu Li, Wu Wei Zi and Ma Huang Gen
Spontaneous sweating → remove Huang Lian, Huang Qin and Huang Bai; add Dang Shen, Fu Xiao Mai and Bai Zhu
With Damp-Heat → add Zhi Zi, Liu Yi San and Che Qian Zi
With tinnitus and dizziness → add Long Dan Cao and Ci Shi

modifications_zh: 虛火較輕：減黃連、黃芩，加知母。
陰虛陽亢：加白芍、龜板。
盜汗甚者：加煅龍骨、煅牡蠣、五味子、麻黃根。
自汗：減黃連、黃芩、黃柏，加黨參、浮小麥、白朮。
兼濕熱：加梔子、六一散、車前子。
兼耳鳴眩暈：加龍膽草、磁石。
modifications_en: For mild deficiency fire, remove Huang Lian and Huang Qin, and add Zhi Mu.
For excess yang rising with yin deficiency, add Bai Shao and Gui Ban.
For severe night sweats, add Duan Long Gu, Duan Mu Li, Wu Wei Zi, and Ma Huang Gen.
For spontaneous sweats, remove Huang Lian, Huang Qin, and Huang Bai, and add Dang Shen, Fu Xiao Mai, and Bai Zhu.
With damp-heat, add Zhi Zi, Liu Yi San, and Che Qian Zi.
With tinnitus and dizziness, add Long Dan Cao and Ci Shi.

modifications_zh: 兼風寒 → 加蔥白、淡豆豉
重症 → 加西瓜霜、淡竹葉
心煩甚 → 加梔子、淡竹葉
氣陰兩傷 → 加西洋參
血淋 → 加白茅根、小薊
膀胱炎或尿道炎 → 加黃柏、金錢草
暑熱傷津無濕 → 以半量石膏易滑石
口渴甚、舌紅屬陰津虧虛 → 加麥冬、沙參、石斛、知母
modifications_en: With Wind-Cold → add Cong Bai and Dan Dou Chi
Severe cases → add Xi Gua Shuang and Dan Zhu Ye
Severe irritability → add Zhi Zi and Dan Zhu Ye
Injury to Qi and Yin → add Xi Yang Shen
Bloody Lin syndrome → add Bai Mao Gen and Xiao Ji
Cystitis or urethritis → add Huang Bai and Jin Qian Cao
Dry summerheat → substitute Shi Gao at half the dosage for Hua Shi
Severe thirst and red tongue from Yin-fluid deficiency → add Mai Dong, Sha Shen, Shi Hu and Zhi Mu

modifications_zh: 兼風寒：加蔥白、淡豆豉。
重症：加西瓜霜、淡竹葉。
煩躁甚：加梔子、淡竹葉。
氣陰兩傷：加西洋參。
血淋：加白茅根、小薊。
膀胱炎或尿道炎：加黃柏、金錢草。
燥暑：以半量石膏易滑石。
口渴甚、舌紅、陰液虧虛：加麥冬、沙參、石斛、知母。
modifications_en: For accompanying wind-cold, add Cong Bai and Dan Dou Chi.
For severe cases, add Xi Gua Shuang and Dan Zhu Ye.
For severe irritability, add Zhi Zi and Dan Zhu Ye.
For injury to qi and yin, add Xi Yang Shen.
For bloody lin (painful urinary) symptoms, add Bai Mao Gen and Xiao Ji.
For cystitis or urethritis, add Huang Bai and Jin Qian Cao.
For dry summerheat, substitute Shi Gao at half the dosage for Hua Shi.
For severe thirst with a red tongue from yin-fluid deficiency, add Mai Dong, Sha Shen, Shi Hu, and Zhi Mu.

modifications_zh: 脈細數、口唇舌乾燥 → 加玄參、麥冬、生地
陽明經腑同病 → 加石膏、知母
脈沉澀、舌暗紅、夜間發熱 → 加桃仁、赤芍、當歸
脹滿甚 → 加萊菔子
modifications_en: Thready rapid pulse with dry mouth, lips and tongue → add Xuan Shen, Mai Dong and Sheng Di
Concurrent Yangming channel and organ stage → add Shi Gao and Zhi Mu
Deep hesitant pulse, dark red tongue and fever at night → add Tao Ren, Chi Shao and Dang Gui
Severe distension and fullness → add Lai Fu Zi

modifications_zh: 脈細數、口乾唇燥舌乾：加玄參、麥冬、生地黃。
陽明經證與腑證並見：加石膏、知母。
脈沉澀、舌暗紅、夜間發熱：加桃仁、赤芍、當歸。
脹滿甚者：加萊菔子。
modifications_en: For a thready rapid pulse with dry mouth, lips, and tongue, add Xuan Shen, Mai Dong, and Sheng Di.
For a concurrent Yangming channel and organ stage, add Shi Gao and Zhi Mu.
For a deep hesitant pulse, dark red tongue, and fever at night, add Tao Ren, Chi Shao, and Dang Gui.
For severe distension and fullness, add Lai Fu Zi.

contraindications_zh: 孕婦禁用
邪尚在衛分或太陽表證階段者禁用
心下痞硬，提示邪尚在膈上者禁用
面赤為熱浮於表者禁用
脾胃虛弱、食量甚少者禁用
不能進食者禁用
邪在少陽、頻頻嘔吐者禁用
裡寒脈遲者禁用
自汗出而小便自利者禁用
體虛者須極慎用,宜加補益之品
這個藥方作用強烈，可能會引起嘔吐或腹瀉，虛弱的患者應該特別小心使用。孕婦嚴禁使用。由於這是一種強效的通便藥，對於氣虛（身體能量不足）、陰液不足、便秘不嚴重的患者，特別是年老或體弱者，應該謹慎使用。
使用此藥時，應該注意一旦症狀緩解就停止服用，以免過度使用而損傷身體正氣。如果患者的身體虛弱、脈象沉弱或胃腸中沒有積熱，則不適合使用，否則可能會對身體造成傷害。
contraindications_en: Contraindicated during pregnancy.
Contraindicated when a pathogen remains at the protective (Wei) stage or in the Tai Yang level.
Contraindicated when there is hardness in the epigastric area indicating that the pathogen is still above the diaphragm.
Contraindicated when there is a flushed face due to Heat Floating in the Exterior.
Contraindicated for those with Spleen and Stomach Deficiency who eat only small amounts.
Contraindicated for those who are unable to eat.
Contraindicated for those who vomit frequently due to the pathogen remaining in the Shao Yang.
Contraindicated for those who have Interior Cold with a slow pulse.
Contraindicated for those with spontaneous sweating and normal urination.
Use extreme caution with weak patients, add tonics.

This formula is strong in action and may cause vomiting or diarrhea; weak patients should use it with particular care. Strictly contraindicated in pregnancy. As a potent purgative, use cautiously in patients with Qi deficiency, insufficient Yin fluids, or constipation that is not severe — especially the elderly or debilitated.

Note that the formula should be discontinued as soon as symptoms improve, to avoid injuring the upright Qi through overuse. It is unsuitable for patients who are weak, whose pulse is deep and feeble, or who lack accumulated heat in the stomach and intestines; otherwise it may cause harm.

contraindications_en: This formula is strongly purgative and may cause vomiting or diarrhea; weak patients should use it with particular care. It is strictly contraindicated during pregnancy. As a powerful purgative, it should be used cautiously in those with Qi Deficiency, insufficient Yin fluids, or mild constipation, especially the elderly and debilitated.

Discontinue as soon as the symptoms resolve, so that overuse does not damage the upright Qi. It is not appropriate for those with a weak constitution, a deep, weak pulse, or no heat accumulation in the Stomach and Intestines, as it may otherwise cause harm.

modifications_zh: 桂枝(按病情加減)：辛散下焦蓄血，與桃仁合用可以加強活血化瘀之效。
桃仁(按病情加減)：甘緩解小腹急結，與桂枝合用可以加強活血化瘀之效。
黃連(按病情加減)：清熱燥濕，瀉火解毒。
犀角(按病情加減)：清熱涼血，解毒定驚。
註：以上藥物用量為古代用量，現代應用需根據患者具體情況調整。加入桂枝、桃仁是用於治療大熱之氣，熱甚搏血的情況。加入黃連、犀角用於疏利三焦，徹其本熱。
modifications_en: Gui Zhi (Cinnamon Twig, add per pattern): acrid, disperses accumulated Blood in the Lower Jiao; combined with Tao Ren it strengthens the effect of invigorating Blood and resolving stasis.
Tao Ren (Peach Kernel, add per pattern): sweet, relieves acute binding/tension in the lower abdomen; combined with Gui Zhi it strengthens the effect of invigorating Blood and resolving stasis.
Huang Lian (Coptis Rhizome, add per pattern): clears Heat, dries Dampness, drains Fire and relieves toxicity.

Xi Jiao (Rhinoceros Horn, add per pattern — a historical classical ingredient; modern practice substitutes Shui Niu Jiao/Water Buffalo Horn): clears Heat, cools the Blood, relieves toxicity and settles fright.

Note: the dosages above reflect classical usage; modern application must be adjusted to the patient's specific condition. Gui Zhi and Tao Ren are added to treat intense Heat forcing the Blood; Huang Lian and Xi Jiao are added to course the Triple Burner and thoroughly clear the underlying Heat.

modifications_zh: 術後或外傷後便秘：加桃仁、當歸。
痔瘡：加槐花、槐角。
產後便秘：加熟地黃、當歸、何首烏。

modifications_en: For post-surgical or post-injury constipation, add Tao Ren and Dang Gui.
For hemorrhoids, add Huai Hua and Huai Jiao.
For postpartum constipation, add Shu Di, Dang Gui, and He Shou Wu.
For habitual constipation, add Yu Li Ren.
For post-apoplexy constipation, add Gua Lou, Sheng Di, and Rou Cong Rong.

contraindications_zh: 孕婦禁用
血虛便秘者，宜加減使用
體質甚虛者，宜加減使用
本方雖為潤腸緩下之劑，但含有攻下破滯之品，故年老體虛，津虧血少者，不宜常服，孕婦慎用。
對麻子仁過敏者禁用：如果對麻子仁過敏，應避免服用麻子仁丸。
不宜久服：麻子仁丸雖具有潤腸通便的功效，但不宜久服。
麻子仁是大麻的種子，需要驗尿者不宜服用。
contraindications_en: Contraindicated during pregnancy.
Modify for treating constipation with Blood Deficiency.
Modify for treating the very weak.

Although this formula moistens the intestines and gently purges, it contains purgative, stagnation-breaking ingredients; the elderly and weak, and those with depleted fluids and scanty Blood, should not take it regularly. Use with caution in pregnancy.
Contraindicated for those allergic to Ma Zi Ren: anyone allergic to hemp seed should avoid taking Ma Zi Ren Wan.
Not for long-term use: although Ma Zi Ren Wan moistens the intestines and unblocks the bowels, it should not be taken over a long period.
Ma Zi Ren is the seed of Cannabis sativa; those who must undergo urine drug testing should not take it.

contraindications_zh: 本方雖為潤腸緩下之劑，但含有攻下破滯之品，故年老體虛，津虧血少者，不宜常服，孕婦慎用。
對麻子仁過敏者禁用：如果對麻子仁過敏，應避免服用麻子仁丸。
不宜久服：麻子仁丸雖具有潤腸通便的功效，但不宜久服。
麻子仁是大麻的種子，需要驗尿者不宜服用。
孕婦禁用。
治療血虛便秘時須加減使用。
治療極度虛弱者時須加減使用。
contraindications_en: Although this is a moistening, mild laxative formula, it contains harsh, stagnation-breaking ingredients; the elderly and weak and those with depleted fluids and scant Blood should not take it regularly, and it should be used with caution during pregnancy.
Contraindicated for those allergic to hemp seed (Ma Zi Ren); anyone with such an allergy should avoid taking Ma Zi Ren Wan.
Not for long-term use: although Ma Zi Ren Wan moistens the Intestines and unblocks the bowels, it should not be taken for prolonged periods.
Ma Zi Ren is the seed of Cannabis sativa; those subject to urine drug testing should not take this formula.
Contraindicated during pregnancy.
Modify for treating constipation with Blood Deficiency.
Modify for treating the very weak.

modifications_zh: 濕熱較重：加蒲公英、梔子、鬱金。
腹痛劇烈：加延胡索、香附、川楝子。
食慾不振、便溏：加蒼朮、厚朴、陳皮、雞內金。
體質虛弱：加太子參、當歸。
modifications_en: For severe damp-heat, add Pu Gong Ying, Zhi Zi, and Yu Jin.
For severe abdominal pain, add Yan Hu Suo, Xiang Fu, and Chuan Lian Zi.
For poor appetite with loose stools, add Cang Zhu, Hou Po, Chen Pi, and Ji Nei Jin.
For a weak constitution, add Tai Zi Shen and Dang Gui.

main_value.formula_song_zh:
大柴胡湯用大黃，枳芩夏芍棗生薑，
少陽陽明同合病，和解攻裡效無雙。
main_value.formula_song:
大柴胡湯用大黃，枳芩夏芍棗生薑，
少陽陽明同合病，和解攻裡效無雙。

pattern_indications_zh: 太陽少陽合病：微惡寒、發熱、肢體酸痛、心下支結、嘔吐、苔薄白、脈弦或浮大。
pattern_indications_en: Combined Tai Yang–Shao Yang disease: slight aversion to cold, fever, generalized body aches, focal distention/discomfort below the Heart, vomiting, thin white tongue coating, wiry or floating-large pulse.

pattern_indications_zh: 太陽少陽合病：微惡寒、發熱、肢體酸痛、心下支結、嘔吐、苔薄白、脈弦或浮大。
pattern_indications_en: Combined Taiyang–Shaoyang pattern: slight aversion to cold, fever, aching limbs, focal (support-like) distention below the heart, vomiting; thin white coating; pulse wiry, or floating and large.

branch_value.in_formula_zh: 透解少陽之邪，疏泄氣機之鬱滯，為和解少陽之君藥。
branch_value.actions_zh: 和解少陽退熱，疏肝解鬱，升舉陽氣。
branch_value.in_formula_en: Chief: vents Shaoyang and moves constrained Qi (from the Xiao Chai Hu Tang base).
branch_value.actions_en: Harmonizes Shaoyang, resolves fever, courses the Liver and raises clear Yang.
branch_value.role_reason_zh: 君藥，本方為小柴胡湯與桂枝湯合方，柴胡仍為君藥。

branch_value.decoction_reference_g: 3-10g（外感）/9-15g（痹痛）— 藥材通用範圍，課件未列本方專屬劑量
branch_value.in_formula_zh: 本方加桂枝湯之君藥而成，解肌發表，兼顧太陽表證未罷。
branch_value.actions_zh: 解肌發表，調和營衛，溫通經脈，助陽化氣。
branch_value.in_formula_en: Deputy (added — Gui Zhi Tang's chief herb): releases the muscle layer for the unresolved exterior aspect.
branch_value.actions_en: Releases the muscle layer, harmonizes Ying/Wei and warms the channels.
branch_value.role_reason_zh: 本方在小柴胡湯基礎上加桂枝湯君臣藥對（桂枝、芍藥），課件列為「Add chief pair of Gui Zhi Tang」。

branch_value.in_formula_zh: 清泄少陽之熱，與柴胡相配為和解少陽之主要藥對。
branch_value.actions_zh: 清熱燥濕，瀉火解毒。
branch_value.in_formula_en: Deputy: clears Shaoyang Heat, paired with Chai Hu (from the Xiao Chai Hu Tang base).
branch_value.actions_en: Clears Heat, dries Dampness and drains Fire.
branch_value.role_reason_zh: 臣藥，來自小柴胡湯（課件 Table92）。

branch_value.decoction_reference_g: 5-30g — 藥材通用範圍，課件未列本方專屬劑量
branch_value.in_formula_zh: 本方加桂枝湯之臣藥而成，與桂枝相配調和營衛，緩急止痛。
branch_value.actions_zh: 養血調經，斂陰止汗，柔肝止痛，平抑肝陽。
branch_value.in_formula_en: Deputy (added — Gui Zhi Tang's deputy herb): harmonizes Ying/Wei with Gui Zhi and relieves spasm/pain.
branch_value.actions_en: Nourishes Blood, harmonizes Ying/Wei and relieves spasmodic pain.
branch_value.role_reason_zh: 與桂枝同為加入的桂枝湯藥對。

branch_value.in_formula_zh: 和胃降逆，化痰散結，為小柴胡湯原有佐藥。
branch_value.actions_zh: 燥濕化痰，降逆和胃止嘔，消痞散結。
branch_value.in_formula_en: Assistant: harmonizes the Stomach and transforms Phlegm (from the Xiao Chai Hu Tang base).
branch_value.actions_en: Dries Dampness, transforms Phlegm and directs Qi downward.
branch_value.role_reason_zh: 佐藥，來自小柴胡湯。

branch_value.in_formula_zh: 扶正補中，防邪深入，為小柴胡湯原有佐藥。
branch_value.actions_zh: 大補元氣，補脾益肺，生津止渴。
branch_value.in_formula_en: Assistant: supports and protects Middle Qi (from the Xiao Chai Hu Tang base).
branch_value.actions_en: Strongly tonifies Qi and supports Spleen/Lung/Heart.
branch_value.role_reason_zh: 佐藥，來自小柴胡湯。

branch_value.in_formula_zh: 溫胃止嘔，助半夏和胃，兼助桂枝解表。
branch_value.actions_zh: 解表散寒，溫中止嘔，化痰止咳。
branch_value.in_formula_en: Assistant: warms the Stomach and stops nausea, works with Ban Xia; also assists Gui Zhi in releasing the exterior.
branch_value.actions_en: Disperses exterior Cold, warms the Middle and stops vomiting.
branch_value.role_reason_zh: 佐藥，來自小柴胡湯，兼助桂枝湯解表。

branch_value.in_formula_zh: 扶助脾胃，調和營衛。
branch_value.actions_zh: 補中益氣，養血安神，緩和藥性。
branch_value.in_formula_en: Assistant: supports Qi and harmonizes the other herbs.
branch_value.actions_en: Tonifies Spleen/Stomach Qi and calms the Spirit.
branch_value.role_reason_zh: 佐藥，來自小柴胡湯，兼助桂枝湯調和營衛。

branch_value.in_formula_zh: 益氣和中，調和諸藥。
branch_value.actions_zh: 補脾和胃，益氣復脈。
branch_value.in_formula_en: Envoy: supports Qi and harmonizes the formula (from the Xiao Chai Hu Tang base).
branch_value.actions_en: Tonifies the Middle and harmonizes all the other herbs.
branch_value.role_reason_zh: 使藥，來自小柴胡湯（課件標為使藥）。

main_value.granule_concentration_ratio: 5:1 濃縮顆粒 (順天堂 官網: https://www.sunten.com.tw/)

main_value.actions_en: Harmonize Shaoyang and Reduce Fever; Course Liver Qi and Relieve Constraint; Raise Clear Yang Qi; Disperse Wind-Heat and Resolve Phlegm

contraindications_en: Use with caution during pregnancy.
Use with caution for those with Qi Stagnation with underlying Liver and Kidney Yin Deficiency.

Liver constraint mostly arises from unfulfilled emotions; the person taking this formula must also work at the psychological level to release stress for it to be effective. Otherwise the medicine is 'free and easy' (xiao yao) while the person is not, and the benefit will be limited.

modifications_en: For heat predominating over cold, increase Huang Qin and Huang Lian.
For pronounced turbidity with acid coming up, increase Ban Xia.
For cold predominating over heat, increase Gan Jiang.
For a thick, greasy tongue coating with severe dry heaves and no middle qi deficiency, remove Ren Shen and Da Zao and add Zhi Shi and Sheng Jiang.

modifications_zh: 嘔吐甚 → 加生薑，去白朮
寒甚 → 加附子、肉桂
兼心悸 → 加茯苓
腹滿 → 加附子，去白朮

modifications_en: Severe vomiting → add Sheng Jiang; remove Bai Zhu
Severe cold → add Fu Zi and Rou Gui
With palpitations → add Fu Ling
Abdominal fullness → add Fu Zi; remove Bai Zhu

Bleeding from Yang deficiency → add Ai Ye, Huang Qi and E Jiao; replace Gan Jiang with Pao Jiang

modifications_zh: 嘔吐劇烈：加生薑，減白朮。
寒甚：加附子、肉桂。
心悸：加茯苓。
腹滿：加附子，減白朮。
腹痛劇烈：加重人參用量。
陽虛失血：加艾葉、黃耆、阿膠，並以炮薑易乾薑。
modifications_en: For severe vomiting, add Sheng Jiang and remove Bai Zhu.
For severe cold, add Fu Zi and Rou Gui.
For palpitations, add Fu Ling.
For abdominal fullness, add Fu Zi and remove Bai Zhu.
For severe abdominal pain, increase the dosage of Ren Shen.
For bleeding due to yang deficiency, add Ai Ye, Huang Qi, and E Jiao, and replace Gan Jiang with Pao Jiang.

modifications_zh: 寒甚 → 加川椒，以肉桂易桂枝
便溏 → 加白朮、白扁豆
兼氣滯 → 加木香、陳皮
蟲積 → 加烏梅、川椒，減飴糖、白芍
modifications_en: More severe cold → add Chuan Jiao; substitute Rou Gui for Gui Zhi
Loose stools → add Bai Zhu and Bai Bian Dou
With Qi stagnation → add Mu Xiang and Chen Pi
Parasites → add Wu Mei and Chuan Jiao; reduce Yi Tang and Bai Shao

modifications_zh: 寒較甚：加川椒，並以肉桂易桂枝。
便溏：加白朮、白扁豆。
兼氣滯：加木香、陳皮。
蟲積：加烏梅、川椒，並減飴糖、白芍用量。
modifications_en: For more severe cold, add Chuan Jiao and substitute Rou Gui for Gui Zhi.
For loose stools, add Bai Zhu and Bai Bian Dou.
For accompanying qi stagnation, add Mu Xiang and Chen Pi.
For parasites, add Wu Mei and Chuan Jiao, and reduce Yi Tang and Bai Shao.

contraindications_zh: 陰虛火旺者慎用。
因嘔吐或蛔蟲所致者，宜去甘味藥。
腹脹（中滿）者宜隨證加減。
contraindications_en: Contraindicated for those with Heat from Yin Deficiency.
Eliminate sweet flavor for vomiting or roundworms.
Modify for abdominal distention.

contraindications_zh: 陰虛火旺，嘔吐及中滿者慎用

Weak constitution with a frail pulse → add Hong Shen and Huang Qi
Severe cold with excessive sweating and severe diarrhea → increase Fu Zi and Gan Jiang; add Long Gu and Mu Li
Intractable Bi syndrome → add Gui Zhi and Bai Zhu

modifications_zh: 虛寒所致水腫、帶下：加黨參、茯苓、澤瀉。
腰痛：加桑寄生、杜仲。
體質虛弱、脈微弱：加紅參、黃耆。
寒甚、汗出過多、下利劇烈：加重附子、乾薑用量，加龍骨、牡蠣。
頑固痺證：加桂枝、白朮。
modifications_en: For edema or leukorrhea from deficiency cold, add Dang Shen, Fu Ling, and Ze Xie.
For low back pain, add Sang Ji Sheng and Du Zhong.
For a weak constitution with a frail pulse, add Hong Shen and Huang Qi.
For severe cold, excessive sweating, and severe diarrhea, increase Fu Zi and Gan Jiang and add Long Gu and Mu Li.
For intractable painful obstruction (bi) symptoms, add Gui Zhi and Bai Zhu.

branch_value.formula_song_zh:
苓朮參甘四味同。方名君子取謙沖。
增來陳夏痰涎滌。再入香砂痞滿通。
水穀精微陰以化。陽和布護氣斯充。
若刪半夏六君內。錢氏書中有異功。

main_value.formula_song_zh:
四君子湯中和義，參朮茯苓甘草比，
益以夏陳名六君，祛痰補氣陽虛餌。
main_value.formula_song:

益以夏陳名六君，祛痰補氣陽虛餌。

modifications_zh: 裏寒腹痛泄瀉 → 加乾薑、肉桂
濕熱泄瀉 → 加黃連、車前子、澤瀉
消化不良、納差 → 加神麴、麥芽、山楂
經行泄瀉 → 加香附、木香
modifications_en: Diarrhea with cramps due to interior cold → add Gan Jiang and Rou Gui
Diarrhea due to Damp-Heat → add Huang Lian, Che Qian Zi and Ze Xie
Poor digestion and anorexia → add Shen Qu, Mai Ya and Shan Zha
Diarrhea with the onset of menstrual flow → add Xiang Fu and Mu Xiang

modifications_zh: 裡寒所致腹瀉伴絞痛：加乾薑、肉桂。
濕熱泄瀉：加黃連、車前子、澤瀉。
消化不良、食慾不振：加神麴、麥芽、山楂。
經行泄瀉（腹瀉隨月經而作）：加香附、木香。
modifications_en: For diarrhea with cramps due to internal cold, add Gan Jiang and Rou Gui.
For diarrhea due to damp-heat, add Huang Lian, Che Qian Zi, and Ze Xie.
For poor digestion and anorexia, add Shen Qu, Mai Ya, and Shan Zha.
For diarrhea with the onset of menstrual flow, add Xiang Fu and Mu Xiang.

contraindications_zh: 實證者禁用
兼陰虛內熱者，宜加減使用
孕婦慎用
表裡有熱者慎用
服用本方，禁食生冷、油膩、不易消化之物
contraindications_en: Contraindicated for those with Excess syndromes.
Modify for concurrent Heat from Yin Deficiency.
Use with caution during pregnancy.
Use with caution for those with Exterior or Interior Heat conditions.
While taking this formula, avoid raw, cold, greasy, and hard-to-digest foods.

modifications_zh: 四物湯劑量加減方法：若有氣虛的症狀，可以加人參、黃芪〔字損〕藥物來補氣並幫助生血。若血瘀較為嚴重，可加桃仁、紅花，並將白芍改為赤芍，以增強活血化瘀的效果。若血虛又兼有怕冷或手腳冰冷的情況，可以加肉桂、炮薑和吳茱萸，以溫暖血脈。若血虛又伴隨內熱，可加黃芩、丹皮，並將熟地改為生地，以清熱涼血。若用於懷孕中的胎動不安或出血，可加阿膠、艾葉來止血並安胎。
四物湯中藥材劑量原則上是等分，但可以根據個人情況靈活調整。比如，《蒲輔周醫療經驗》建議川芎的劑量可以減少，通常為當歸的一半，地黃則可以增加到當歸的兩倍。
《銳齋醫學講稿》也提到，若主要是補血作用，熟地和當歸的劑量可偏重，白芍次之；若不使用熟地，則白芍的劑量可高於當歸。這些經驗可作為調配四物湯的參考。
modifications_en: Dose adjustments: for Qi deficiency add Ren Shen and Huang Qi to tonify Qi and generate Blood; for marked Blood Stasis add Tao Ren and Hong Hua and substitute Chi Shao for Bai Shao; for Blood deficiency with cold or cold extremities add Rou Gui, Pao Jiang and Wu Zhu Yu; for Blood deficiency with interior Heat add Huang Qin and Mu Dan Pi and substitute Sheng Di for Shu Di; for restless fetus or bleeding in pregnancy add E Jiao and Ai Ye.
The four herbs are classically used in equal parts but the ratio is adjusted per patient: 蒲輔周 recommends halving Chuan Xiong relative to Dang Gui and doubling Di Huang relative to Dang Gui.
銳齋醫學講稿: when tonifying Blood is the main aim, weight Shu Di and Dang Gui heavier and Bai Shao next; if Shu Di is omitted, Bai Shao may exceed Dang Gui.

contraindications_zh: 用於慢性病，但是不嚴重者。不能用於急性嚴重失血或其他血虛，包括嚴重的虛弱，此時應補氣(當歸補血湯)。
本方中的熟地性質黏滯、當歸性滑潤，因此對於濕氣較重、容易中滿、腹脹或大便稀溏的患者不宜使用。
急性嚴重失血者禁用
嚴重虛弱或呼吸費力者禁用
素體脾陽虛者須加減後使用
脫水者禁用
脾胃虛弱者慎用——熟地黃性質滋膩礙運
氣血暴脫者禁用
孕婦慎用
contraindications_en: For chronic conditions that are not severe. Not for acute severe blood loss or other Blood deficiency with severe debility, in which case tonify Qi instead (Dang Gui Bu Xue Tang).

Shu Di Huang in this formula is sticky and cloying and Dang Gui is slippery and moistening; therefore it is not suitable for patients with pronounced dampness, tendency to epigastric fullness, abdominal distension, or loose stools.
Contraindicated for those with acute, severe blood loss.
Contraindicated for those with severe weakness or labored breathing.
Modify for those with constitutional Spleen Yang Deficiency.
Contraindicated for those with dehydration.
Use with caution for those with Spleen and Stomach Deficiency due to the Stagnating nature of Shu Di Huang.
Contraindicated for those with Blood or Qi collapse.
Use with caution during pregnancy.

modifications_zh: 水瀉：加罌粟殼、訶子。
腰膝痠冷：加附子、肉桂。
中氣下陷脫肛：加黃耆、升麻、人參。
腹脹：加木香、小茴香。
裡寒腹痛嘔惡：合理中丸。
modifications_en: For watery diarrhea, add Ying Su Ke and He Zi.
For sore and cold lower back and extremities, add Fu Zi and Rou Gui.
For prolapsed rectum from middle qi sinking, add Huang Qi, Sheng Ma, and Ren Shen.
For abdominal distention, add Mu Xiang and Xiao Hui Xiang.
For interior cold with abdominal pain and nausea, combine with Li Zhong Wan.

modifications_zh: 加減法：若心煩不眠，屬肝血不足，陰虛內熱較甚者，合二至丸或加生地黃、玄參、白芍等，以養血滋陰清熱。兼見盜汗甚者，加五味子、白芍、浮小麥以安神斂汗。
心悸較重者，加龍齒、龜甲、珍珠母等以鎮驚安神。心悸多夢，時有驚醒，舌淡，脈細弦，屬心膽氣虛者，可加黨參、龍齒以益氣鎮驚。如精神抑鬱，心煩不眠較甚者，可合甘麥大棗湯加夜交藤、合歡皮以緩肝安神解鬱，或加入合歡花、夜交藤、石菖蒲、鬱金等解鬱安神之品，療效更好。
modifications_en: Modifications: for vexation and insomnia due to Liver Blood deficiency with pronounced Yin-deficiency internal Heat, combine with Er Zhi Wan or add Sheng Di Huang (Fresh Rehmannia Root), Xuan Shen (Scrophularia Root) and Bai Shao (White Peony Root) to nourish Blood, enrich Yin and clear Heat. If night sweating is marked, add Wu Wei Zi (Schisandra Fruit), Bai Shao and Fu Xiao Mai (Floating Wheat) to calm the Spirit and astringe sweating.

For more pronounced palpitations, add Long Chi (Fossilized Teeth), Gui Ban (Tortoise Shell) and Zhen Zhu Mu (Mother-of-Pearl) to settle fright and calm the Spirit. For palpitations with dream-disturbed sleep, occasional startled waking, pale tongue and thin wiry pulse due to Heart-Gallbladder Qi deficiency, add Dang Shen (Codonopsis Root) and Long Chi to tonify Qi and settle fright. For depression with marked vexation and insomnia, combine with Gan Mai Da Zao Tang and add Ye Jiao Teng (Polygonum Multiflorum Stem) and He Huan Pi (Albizzia Bark) to soothe the Liver, calm the Spirit and relieve constraint; adding He Huan Hua (Albizzia Flower), Ye Jiao Teng, Shi Chang Pu (Acorus Rhizome) and Yu Jin (Curcuma Tuber) further improves the effect of relieving constraint and calming the Spirit.

modifications_en: Modifications: for vexed insomnia from Liver Blood deficiency with pronounced Yin-deficiency internal Heat, combine with Er Zhi Wan, or add Sheng Di Huang, Xuan Shen and Bai Shao to nourish Blood, enrich Yin and clear Heat. With severe night sweats, add Wu Wei Zi, Bai Shao and Fu Xiao Mai to calm the spirit and restrain sweating.

For pronounced palpitations, add Long Chi, Gui Jia and Zhen Zhu Mu to settle fright and calm the spirit. For palpitations with copious dreaming and frequent startled waking, pale tongue and thin wiry pulse (Heart–Gallbladder qi deficiency), add Dang Shen and Long Chi to augment qi and settle fright. modifications_zh: 氣鬱甚：重用香附，加木香、檳榔、枳實。
濕鬱甚：重用蒼朮，加茯苓、澤瀉。
食鬱甚：重用神麴，加麥芽、山楂。
血鬱甚：重用川芎，加桃仁、紅花。
火鬱甚：重用梔子，加黃連、青黛。
痰鬱甚：重用蒼朮，加膽南星、瓜蔞。
無火鬱：減梔子（無濕鬱減蒼朮，無食鬱減神麴）。
modifications_en: For severe qi constraint, increase the amount of Xiang Fu and add Mu Xiang, Bing Lang, and Zhi Shi.
For severe damp constraint, increase the amount of Cang Zhu and add Fu Ling and Ze Xie.
For severe food constraint, increase the amount of Shen Qu and add Mai Ya and Shan Zha.
For severe blood constraint, increase the amount of Chuan Xiong and add Tao Ren and Hong Hua.
For severe fire constraint, increase the amount of Zhi Zi and add Huang Lian and Qing Dai.
For severe phlegm constraint, increase the amount of Cang Zhu and add Dan Nan Xing and Gua Lou.
In the absence of fire constraint, remove Zhi Zi; likewise remove Cang Zhu when there is no damp constraint and Shen Qu when there is no food constraint.

branch_value.formula_song_zh:
柴胡疏肝芍川芎，陳皮枳殼甘草同。
疏肝理氣止脅痛，肝鬱氣滯服之通。

柴胡疏肝芍川芎，枳殼陳皮草香附，

main_value.formula_song:
柴胡疏肝芍川芎，枳殼陳皮草香附，
疏肝行氣兼活血，脅肋疼痛立能除。

branch_value.in_formula_zh: 祛痰寬胸，開胸散結，滌痰下氣，為治胸痹要藥。
branch_value.actions_zh: 清化熱痰，止咳化痰，清熱瀉火，潤肺，散結。
branch_value.in_formula_en: Chief: expels Phlegm, opens the chest and dissipates clumping (aromatic, sweet, cold).
branch_value.actions_en: Transforms Phlegm-Heat, stops cough, clears Heat, moistens the Lung and dissipates masses.
branch_value.role_reason_zh: 君藥，主治胸痹（痰濁閉阻胸陽）。

branch_value.in_formula_zh: 溫通胸陽，行氣散結，助瓜蔞開胸散結、通陽止痛。
branch_value.actions_zh: 溫通陽氣，行氣，散結止痛。
branch_value.in_formula_en: Deputy: warms Yang, moves Qi and disperses clumping (warm, aromatic).
branch_value.actions_en: Warms Yang, moves Qi, disperses clumps and relieves pain.
branch_value.role_reason_zh: 臣藥，溫通胸陽以助君藥。

branch_value.in_formula_zh: 本方在瓜蔞薤白白酒湯基礎上加半夏而成，加強燥濕化痰、降逆和胃之力，主治痰濁較重、胸痹疼痛較甚者。
branch_value.actions_zh: 燥濕化痰，降逆和胃止嘔，消痞散結。
branch_value.in_formula_en: Assistant (added to the base Gua Lou Xie Bai Bai Jiu Tang): dries Dampness and transforms Phlegm, directs rebellious Qi downward — for more severe Phlegm obstruction with chest pain.
branch_value.actions_en: Dries Dampness, transforms Phlegm, directs rebellious Qi downward and dissolves masses.
branch_value.role_reason_zh: 佐藥，此方較瓜蔞薤白白酒湯多此一味，是兩方鑑別的關鍵。

branch_value.herb_en: White Wine (clear grain spirit, used as decoction vehicle)
branch_value.name_en: White Wine (clear grain spirit, used as decoction vehicle)
branch_value.decoction_reference_g: 作煎煮介質，非固定劑量；同源基礎方（瓜蔞薤白白酒湯）課件載 30–1,400ml，不能飲酒者可減量或省略
branch_value.in_formula_zh: 行氣活血，溫通陽氣，助藥力布散；不勝酒者可酌減或省略。
branch_value.actions_zh: 行氣活血、溫通陽氣，作藥引助藥力布散。
branch_value.in_formula_en: Assistant: used as the decoction vehicle to move Qi/Blood and warm Yang; may be reduced or omitted if wine is contraindicated.
branch_value.actions_en: Moves Qi and Blood, warms Yang; used as a decoction vehicle.
branch_value.role_reason_zh: 佐藥，與水同煎作為煎煮介質。

modifications_zh: 肝氣鬱甚、頻頻嘆息噯氣 → 加香附、青皮、陳皮、瓜蔞、柴胡
咽中如物梗阻甚 → 加桔梗、玄參、甘草、赤芍藥
氣鬱化火、急躁易怒、口苦 → 加黃連、黃芩、梔子
兼氣陰兩虛之失眠、神疲乏力 → 加酸棗仁、牡丹皮、黃耆、沙參
modifications_en: Severe Liver Qi stagnation with frequent sighing and burping → add Xiang Fu, Qing Pi, Chen Pi, Gua Lou and Chai Hu
Severe clumped feeling in the throat → add Jie Geng, Xuan Shen, Gan Cao and Chi Shao Yao
Fire generated by stagnant Qi with short temper, irritability and a bitter taste in the mouth → add Huang Lian, Huang Qin and Zhi Zi
With Qi and Yin deficiency manifesting as insomnia, low spirits and fatigue → add Suan Zao Ren, Mu Dan Pi, Huang Qi and Sha Shen

modifications_zh: 肝氣鬱滯較甚、頻頻嘆息噯氣：加香附、青皮、陳皮、瓜蔞、柴胡。
咽中結滯感較甚：加桔梗、玄參、甘草、赤芍藥。
氣鬱化火而急躁易怒、口苦：加黃連、黃芩、梔子。
兼氣陰兩虛而失眠、情緒低落、疲乏：加酸棗仁、牡丹皮、黃耆、沙參。
modifications_en: For severe liver qi stagnation with frequent sighing and burping, add Xiang Fu, Qing Pi, Chen Pi, Gua Lou, and Chai Hu.
For a severe clumped feeling in the throat, add Jie Geng, Xuan Shen, Gan Cao, and Chi Shao Yao.
For fire generated by stagnant qi with short temper, irritability, and a bitter taste in the mouth, add Huang Lian, Huang Qin, and Zhi Zi.
For concurrent qi and yin deficiency manifesting as insomnia, low spirit, and fatigue, add Suan Zao Ren, Mu Dan Pi, Huang Qi, and Sha Shen.

contraindications_zh: 肺陰虛所致胸痛，見顴紅口苦、舌紅少苔者禁用
氣滯化熱者禁用
不宜長期服用
方中多辛溫苦燥之品，僅適宜於痰氣互結而無熱者。若見顴紅口苦、舌紅少苔屬於氣鬱化火，陰傷津少者，雖具梅核氣之特徵，亦不宜使用本方。陰虛津虧或火旺者不宜使用。
contraindications_en: Contraindicated for those with chest pain due to Lung Yin Deficiency with red cheeks, a bitter taste in the mouth and a red tongue with a scanty coating.
Contraindicated for those with Heat due to Qi Stagnation.
Do not use long term.

The formula contains many acrid-warm, bitter-drying ingredients and is only appropriate for Phlegm and Qi binding without heat. If there are red cheeks, a bitter taste in the mouth, and a red tongue with scanty coating — indicating Qi constraint transforming into Fire with damaged Yin and scanty fluids — this formula should not be used even when plum-pit qi features are present. Not suitable for those with Yin deficiency and fluid depletion or with exuberant Fire.

contraindications_zh: 方中多辛溫苦燥之品，僅適宜於痰氣互結而無熱者。若見顴紅口苦、舌紅少苔屬於氣鬱化火，陰傷津少者，雖具梅核氣之特徵，亦不宜使用本方。陰虛津虧或火旺者不宜使用。
肺陰虛所致胸痛，見顴紅、口苦、舌紅少苔者禁用
氣滯化熱者禁用
不宜長期服用
contraindications_en: This formula consists mostly of acrid-warm, bitter-drying ingredients and is suitable only for Phlegm and Qi binding together without Heat. If there are red cheeks, a bitter taste in the mouth, and a red tongue with scanty coating — indicating constrained Qi transforming into Fire with injured Yin and diminished fluids — this formula should not be used even when the characteristic plum-pit Qi is present. It is not suitable for those with Yin Deficiency with depleted fluids or with exuberant Fire.
Contraindicated for those with chest pain due to Lung Yin Deficiency with red cheeks, a bitter taste in the mouth and a red tongue with a scanty coating.
Contraindicated for those with Heat due to Qi Stagnation.
Do not use long term.

branch_value.in_formula_zh: 理氣和胃，降逆止嘔，與竹茹相配一溫一涼，共為君藥。
branch_value.actions_zh: 理氣健脾，燥濕化痰，降氣止嘔。
branch_value.in_formula_en: Chief (paired with Zhu Ru): regulates Qi, harmonizes the Stomach and stops hiccough/nausea — warm, paired against Zhu Ru's cold.
branch_value.actions_en: Regulates Qi, strengthens the Spleen, dries Dampness and directs Qi downward.
branch_value.role_reason_zh: 君藥之一，與竹茹相配，溫涼並用直達病所。

branch_value.in_formula_zh: 清胃降逆，止嘔止呃，清熱化痰，與橘皮共為君藥。
branch_value.actions_zh: 清化熱痰，清胃熱，止嘔。
branch_value.in_formula_en: Chief (paired with Chen Pi): clears Stomach Heat, calms Stomach Qi and stops hiccough/nausea/vomiting.
branch_value.actions_en: Clears Phlegm-Heat, clears Stomach Heat and stops vomiting.
branch_value.role_reason_zh: 君藥之一，清胃熱以降逆。

branch_value.in_formula_zh: 補益中氣，生津，扶正以助祛邪。
branch_value.actions_zh: 大補元氣，補脾益肺，生津止渴。
branch_value.in_formula_en: Deputy: tonifies Middle Qi and generates fluids.
branch_value.actions_en: Strongly tonifies Qi and supports Spleen/Lung/Heart.

此中藥在中風急性期絕對禁用！本方宜用於病人神志清醒、體溫正常、出血已止、脈象緩弱者。
高血壓者可服用，但陰虛血熱者忌服。
使用本方需久服才能有效，愈後還應繼續服用，以鞏固療效，防止復發，王氏謂：「服此方愈後，藥不可斷，或隔三五日吃一付，或七八日吃一付。」但若中風後半身不遂屬陰虛陽亢，痰阻血瘀，見舌紅苔黃、脈洪大有力者，非本方所宜。
出血風險（特別是與西藥併用時）：陽還五湯中除了黃耆，還有活血化瘀的藥物（如川芎、紅花、桃仁等）。單獨用藥：對於「氣虛血瘀」證是對症的，一般不會引起出血。與西藥併用：如果患者正在服用抗血小板藥（如阿司匹林）或抗凝血劑（如華法林），再疊加使用強效的活血中藥，會顯著增加出血的風險，如牙齦出血、皮下瘀青、甚至內出血。這點務必告知醫師，並密切監測凝血功能。
contraindications_en: Contraindicated immediately after a stroke due to cerebral hemorrhage.
Contraindicated for those with Wind-Stroke with a big, forceful or firm, wiry, forceful pulse.
Contraindicated for those with Yin Deficiency.
Contraindicated for those with Blood Heat.
Contraindicated for those with Phlegm Stagnation.
Contraindicated during pregnancy.
Be sure consciousness is returned and the temperature is normal.
Be sure there is no hemorrhage present and there is a moderate pulse.

Absolutely contraindicated in the acute stage of stroke! This formula is appropriate once the patient is conscious, the temperature is normal, bleeding has stopped, and the pulse is moderate and weak.
May be taken by those with hypertension, but avoid in those with Yin deficiency and Blood heat.

This formula must be taken over a long period to be effective, and should be continued after recovery to consolidate the effect and prevent recurrence. Wang (Qingren) said: 'After recovery with this formula, the medicine must not be stopped; take one packet every three to five days, or one packet every seven to eight days.' However, if post-stroke hemiplegia belongs to Yin deficiency with Yang hyperactivity or Phlegm obstruction with Blood stasis, with a red tongue, yellow coating, and a surging, big, forceful pulse, this formula is not appropriate.

Bleeding risk (especially when combined with Western drugs): besides Huang Qi, this formula contains Blood-invigorating, stasis-transforming herbs (such as Chuan Xiong, Hong Hua, Tao Ren). Used alone for the Qi-deficiency-with-Blood-stasis pattern it is well indicated and generally does not cause bleeding. Combined with Western drugs: if the patient is taking antiplatelet drugs (such as aspirin) or anticoagulants (such as warfarin), adding potent Blood-invigorating Chinese herbs significantly increases the risk of bleeding — bleeding gums, subcutaneous bruising, even internal bleeding. Be sure to inform the physician and closely monitor coagulation function.

contraindications_zh: 血止後應立即停藥
治療期間病人應安靜臥床
虛寒性出血者禁用
本方為急則治標之劑，血止之後，還當審因圖本，方能鞏固療效；對虛寒性出血則不宜使用。本方為散劑，既可內服，也能外用，但應預先制備，使火氣消退，方可使用。方中藥物皆燒炭，但應注意「存性」，否則藥效不確。
contraindications_en: Discontinue as soon as bleeding stops.
The patient must lie quietly during the treatment.
Contraindicated for those with bleeding due to Deficiency and/or Cold.

This formula is a remedy for treating the branch in acute situations; once bleeding stops, seek the cause and address the root to consolidate the effect. It is not appropriate for bleeding of the deficiency-cold type. As a powder it can be taken internally or applied externally, but it should be prepared in advance so the fire qi dissipates before use. The ingredients are all charred, but take care to 'preserve their nature' (cun xing), otherwise the effect is unreliable.

contraindications_zh: 本方為急則治標之劑，血止之後，還當審因圖本，方能鞏固療效；對虛寒性出血則不宜使用。本方為散劑，既可內服，也能外用，但應預先制備，使火氣消退，方可使用。方中藥物皆燒炭，但應注意「存性」，否則藥效不確。
血止後即當停用
治療期間病人須靜臥休息
虛寒性出血者禁用
contraindications_en: This formula is a remedy for treating the branch in urgent conditions; once the bleeding stops, one must still investigate the cause and address the root in order to consolidate the therapeutic effect. It should not be used for bleeding of the Deficiency-Cold type. As a powder, it may be taken internally or applied externally, but it should be prepared in advance so that its Fire Qi has subsided before use. The ingredients are all charred, but care must be taken to 'preserve their nature' when charring, or the effect will be unreliable.
Discontinue as soon as bleeding stops.
The patient must lie quietly during the treatment.
Contraindicated for those with bleeding due to Deficiency and/or Cold.

contraindications_zh: 本方爲活血化淤消癥之方，如正常妊娠下血者則當慎之，孕婦及產後必須格外小心。僅用於有血瘀者。
如婦人宿有癥病又懷孕者，用本方爲良益之法，但用法應從小晝開始，不知漸加，使之下癥而不傷胎。
臨證運用本方，雖屬有故無須，但仍需注意中病即止，不可過服。若陰道下血反多，腰痠腹痛較甚，則非本方所宜，當辨而治之。
contraindications_en: This formula invigorates the Blood, resolves stasis and reduces masses; use with caution for vaginal bleeding during a normal pregnancy — pregnant and postpartum patients require extra caution. Use only in patients with confirmed Blood stasis.

For a woman with a pre-existing abdominal mass who later becomes pregnant, this formula may be used beneficially, but dosing should start small and be increased gradually, so as to reduce the mass without harming the fetus.

Although classical precedent permits use in pregnancy when there is a genuine indication ('having a reason, therefore no harm'), the formula should still be stopped once the condition resolves and not overused. If vaginal bleeding increases, or lower-back soreness and abdominal pain become more severe, this formula is not appropriate and the case should be re-differentiated and treated accordingly.

contraindications_zh: 本方爲活血化淤消癥之方，如正常妊娠下血者則當慎之，孕婦及產後必須格外小心。僅用於有血瘀者。

contraindications_en: This formula moves Blood, transforms stasis and reduces masses; where there is bleeding in a normal pregnancy it must be used with the greatest caution — take special care during pregnancy and postpartum. Use only where Blood stasis is present.

For a woman with a pre-existing abdominal mass (zheng) who is now pregnant, this formula is the fitting method, but begin with a small dose and increase gradually only if there is no response, so the mass is reduced without harming the fetus.

In clinical use, even where indicated, stop once the effect is achieved and do not overdose. If vaginal bleeding increases instead, or low-back soreness and abdominal pain worsen, this formula is not appropriate — re-differentiate and treat accordingly.

contraindications_zh: 脾氣虛、腎虛者宜減量，並可配合補益藥同用

不宜長期服用
大汗傷津、體液耗竭者禁用
嘔吐過度者禁用
腹瀉過度者禁用

本方藥性偏於滲利，劑量及用藥時間必須小心，過量出現頭暈、目眩、口淡、食慾減退。
本方不宜長服，體弱者常與補養脾胃劑合用。
本方傳統劑型為散劑，吞服散後多飲水，至微有汗出為好。現代一般用湯劑熱服，注意不宜久煎，以免減弱滲利之性。如津液耗傷的口渴或小便不利，不宜用本方，陰虛病人慎用。
contraindications_en: With Spleen Qi and Kidney Deficiency limit dosage, may combine with tonics.
For urinary difficulty with Yin Deficiency, protect Yin.
Overdose symptoms: dizziness, vertigo, bland taste, anorexia.
Avoid long term administration.
Contraindicated with depleted body fluids from profuse perspiration.
Excessive vomiting.
Excessive diarrhea.
Damp-Heat Accumulation.
This formula leans toward percolating and draining; dosage and duration of use must be handled carefully — overdose produces dizziness, vertigo, a bland taste in the mouth, and reduced appetite.
This formula is not for long-term use; in weak patients it is often combined with formulas that tonify the Spleen and Stomach.

The traditional form is a powder; after swallowing the powder, drink plenty of water, ideally until slight sweating occurs. Nowadays it is generally taken as a hot decoction; do not decoct for long, lest the percolating-draining property be weakened. Not suitable for thirst or urinary difficulty from damaged fluids; use with caution in Yin-deficient patients.

contraindications_zh: 無熱象者不宜使用
熱盛陰傷嚴重者禁用
濕邪明顯者禁用
若患者內熱過盛，陰津大損，則不宜使用本方。《傷寒論》指出，在陽明病中，如果患者多汗且口渴，則不應使用猪苓湯，因為多汗會導致胃中過於乾燥，而猪苓湯進一步利小便可能會加重病情。如果患者水濕內滯而無陰虛的徵兆，也應避免使用，以防止阿膠的滋膩性質助長濕邪。
contraindications_en: Without Heat.
Abundant Heat and severely damaged Yin.
Pronounced Dampness.

If internal heat is excessive and Yin fluids are greatly damaged, this formula is not suitable. The Shang Han Lun points out that in Yang Ming disease with profuse sweating and thirst, Zhu Ling Tang should not be given, because profuse sweating makes the stomach too dry and further promoting urination with Zhu Ling Tang may worsen the condition. Also avoid it when water-damp collects internally without signs of Yin deficiency, lest the rich, cloying nature of E Jiao reinforce the damp pathogen.

contraindications_en: If internal Heat is excessive and the Yin fluids are greatly damaged, this formula should not be used. The Shang Han Lun points out that in Yangming disease, if the patient sweats profusely and is thirsty, Zhu Ling Tang should not be given, because profuse sweating makes the Stomach too dry, and further promoting urination with Zhu Ling Tang may aggravate the condition. If Water-Damp is retained internally without signs of Yin Deficiency, it should also be avoided, to prevent the rich, cloying nature of E Jiao from assisting the Damp pathogen.

contraindications_zh: 導致頭痛的原因很多，有外感與內傷的不同，對於氣虛、血虛、或肝腎陰虛、肝陽上亢、肝風內動等引起的頭痛，均不宜使用。
contraindications_en: Headache has many causes, both from external invasion and from internal damage; this formula is not suitable for headaches due to Qi deficiency, Blood deficiency, Liver-Kidney Yin deficiency, Liver Yang Rising, or internal stirring of Liver Wind.

contraindications_zh: 導致頭痛的原因很多，有外感與內傷的不同，對於氣虛、血虛、或肝腎陰虛、肝陽上亢、肝風內動等引起的頭痛，均不宜使用。
肝陽上亢頭痛者忌用。
肝風內動頭痛者忌用。
肝腎陰虛者忌用。
氣血兩虛者忌用。
contraindications_en: Headache has many causes, both externally contracted and internally generated; this formula is not appropriate for headaches due to Qi Deficiency, Blood Deficiency, Liver and Kidney Yin Deficiency, Liver Yang Rising, or internal stirring of Liver Wind.
Contraindicated for those with headache due to Liver Yang Rising.
Contraindicated for those with headache due to Liver Wind.
Contraindicated for those with Kidney or Liver Yin Deficiency.
Contraindicated for those with Qi and Blood Deficiencies.

modifications_zh: 加減法：如果肺熱嚴重，壯熱汗出者，宜加重石膏用量，並酌加桑白皮、黃芩、知母以清泄肺熱；表邪偏重，無汗而惡寒，石膏用量宜減輕，酌加薄荷、蘇葉、桑葉等以助解表宣肺之力；痰多氣急，可加葶藶子、枇杷葉以降氣化痰；痰黃稠而胸悶者，宜加瓜蔞、貝母、黃芩、桔梗以清熱化痰，寬胸利膈。
modifications_en: Modifications: for severe Lung Heat with high fever and sweating, increase the dose of Shi Gao (Gypsum) and consider adding Sang Bai Pi (Mulberry Root Bark), Huang Qin (Scutellaria Root) and Zhi Mu (Anemarrhena Rhizome) to clear and drain Lung Heat. For a predominant exterior pathogen with no sweating and aversion to cold, reduce the dose of Shi Gao and consider adding Bo He (Mint), Su Ye (Perilla Leaf) or Sang Ye (Mulberry Leaf) to assist in releasing the exterior and diffusing Lung Qi. For copious phlegm with rapid breathing, add Ting Li Zi (Lepidium Seed) and Pi Pa Ye (Loquat Leaf) to direct Qi downward and transform Phlegm. For thick yellow phlegm with chest oppression, add Gua Lou (Trichosanthes Fruit), Bei Mu (Fritillaria Bulb), Huang Qin and Jie Geng (Platycodon Root) to clear Heat, transform Phlegm and open the chest.

modifications_zh: 加減法：如果肺熱嚴重，壯熱汗出者，宜加重石膏用量，並酌加桑白皮、黃芩、知母以清泄肺熱；表邪偏重，無汗而惡寒，石膏用量宜減輕，酌加薄荷、蘇葉、桑葉等以助解表宣肺之力；痰多氣急，可加葶藶子、枇杷葉以降氣化痰；痰黃稠而胸悶者，宜加瓜蔞、貝母、黃芩、桔梗以清熱化痰，寬胸利膈。
modifications_en: Modifications: for severe Lung Heat with high fever and sweating, increase Shi Gao and add Sang Bai Pi, Huang Qin and Zhi Mu to clear and drain Lung Heat. Where the exterior pathogen predominates, with no sweating and aversion to cold, lighten Shi Gao and add Bo He, Su Ye and Sang Ye to help release the exterior and diffuse the Lung. For copious phlegm with hasty breathing, add Ting Li Zi and Pi Pa Ye to descend qi and transform phlegm. For thick yellow sputum with chest oppression, add Gua Lou, Bei Mu, Huang Qin and Jie Geng to clear Heat, transform Phlegm, and ease the chest and diaphragm.

contraindications_zh: 本方僅適用於風寒夾痰所致之中風（口眼喎斜、半身不遂）。
若屬氣虛血瘀，或肝風內動之口眼喁斜、半身不遂，不宜使用。
方中白附子和全蠍有一定的毒性，用量宜慎。牽正散雖然有效，但白附子和全蠍均有毒，必須在中醫師的辨證論治指導下使用，嚴格控制劑量，且不宜久服。臨床上常使用經過炮製的藥材以減低毒性，並常配合其他益氣養血、柔肝舒筋的藥物（如黃耆、當歸、地龍等）一起使用，以增強療效、減少副作用，並鞏固根本。
本方偏溫燥。若屬肝陽化風、肝風內動，或氣虛血瘀所致之口眼喎斜、半身不遂者，不宜使用。白附子與全蠍皆有毒，且全方皆使用生品，藥勢較峻烈，劑量不可過大。
孕婦禁用。

contraindications_en: Do not use for deviation of the mouth and eyes or hemiplegia due to Qi Deficiency with Blood Stasis or internal stirring of Liver Wind.

Bai Fu Zi and Quan Xie in this formula are somewhat toxic, so the dosage should be cautious. Although Qian Zheng San is effective, both Bai Fu Zi and Quan Xie are toxic and must be used under the pattern-differentiated guidance of a TCM practitioner, with strict dosage control, and should not be taken long term. In clinical practice, processed forms of the herbs are commonly used to reduce toxicity, and they are often combined with other herbs that tonify Qi, nourish Blood, soften the Liver, and relax the sinews (such as Huang Qi, Dang Gui, and Di Long) to enhance efficacy, reduce side effects, and consolidate the root.

This formula is warm and drying in nature. It should not be used for deviation of the mouth and eyes or hemiplegia due to Liver Yang transforming into Wind, internal stirring of Liver Wind, or Qi Deficiency with Blood Stasis. Bai Fu Zi and Quan Xie are both toxic, and the whole formula uses unprocessed herbs with rather harsh action, so the dosage must not be too large.
This formula should only be used for Wind-Stroke due to Wind-Cold and Phlegm.
Contraindicated unless modified for deviation of the mouth or hemiplegia due to Internal Liver Wind Rising.
Contraindicated unless modified for deviation of the mouth or hemiplegia due to Qi Deficiency and Blood Stagnation.
Bai Fu Zi and Wu Gong are toxic. Do not exceed a dosage of 6gt.
Contraindicated during pregnancy.

modifications_zh: 相關加減法：若咳者，加五味子、乾薑以溫肺散寒止咳。悸者，加桂枝以溫心陽。小便不利者，加茯苓以利小便。腹中痛者，加炮附子以散裡寒。腹瀉者，加薤白以通陽散結。氣鬱甚者，加香附、鬱金以理氣解鬱。有熱者，加梔子、川楝子於以清內熱。
modifications_en: Related modifications: for cough, add Wu Wei Zi (Schisandra Fruit) and Gan Jiang (Dried Ginger) to warm the Lung, disperse Cold and stop cough. For palpitations, add Gui Zhi (Cinnamon Twig) to warm Heart Yang. For difficult urination, add Fu Ling (Poria) to promote urination. For abdominal pain, add prepared Fu Zi (Aconite Root) to disperse interior Cold. For diarrhea, add Xie Bai (Chinese Chive Bulb) to unblock Yang and disperse clumping. For pronounced Qi constraint, add Xiang Fu (Cyperus Rhizome) and Yu Jin (Curcuma Tuber) to regulate Qi and relieve constraint. For Heat, add Zhi Zi (Gardenia Fruit) and Chuan Lian Zi (Toosendan Fruit) to clear internal Heat.

modifications_en: Related modifications: with cough, add Wu Wei Zi and Gan Jiang to warm the Lung, disperse Cold and stop coughing. With palpitations, add Gui Zhi to warm Heart Yang. With inhibited urination, add Fu Ling to promote urination. With abdominal pain, add Pao Fu Zi to disperse internal Cold. With diarrhea, add Xie Bai to unblock Yang and disperse binding. With pronounced qi constraint, add Xiang Fu and Yu Jin to regulate qi and resolve constraint. With Heat signs, add Zhi Zi and Chuan Lian Zi to clear internal Heat.

contraindications_en: This formula is for 'Spleen-deficiency type vaginal discharge'; it is not suitable when the discharge is red-and-white or yellow-red, thick, sticky and foul-smelling, accompanied by signs of Damp-Heat pouring downward such as a red tongue and a rapid pulse.
Contraindicated for those with yellow, bloody, thick, sticky or foul smelling discharge due to Liver Stagnation transforming into Heat or Damp-Heat.

Blazing Stomach fire → add Zhi Zi and Da Huang; substitute Sheng Di for Shu Di

modifications_en: Modifications: for pronounced Fire excess, add herbs such as Shan Dou Gen and Di Gu Pi to strengthen clearing Heat and draining Fire. If Heat in the Blood causes heavier bleeding, remove Shu Di Huang and add herbs such as Niu Bang Zi and Xuan Shen to enhance clearing Heat and cooling the Blood.

**Hu Huang Lian and Huang Lian are two different herbs**: Picrorhiza (clear-deficiency-Heat chapter) versus Coptis (clear-Heat-dry-Damp chapter). The coursework's phrase 'similar to Huang Lian' is a comparison, not an equation.

甘、鹹，寒

branch_value: 清肝明目（課件：與石決明功效相近，列為第二線用藥）
收斂生肌、止癢（外用治濕疹、久不癒瘡瘍）
制酸止痛（功似牡蠣，治胃酸過多、胃痛）

cautions_zh: 課件未列珍珠母的禁忌與注意事項；本卡不代為填寫。珍珠母自身條目（Materia Medica Abbbreviated.md）同樣未列禁忌，僅補齊性味歸經、功效與用量。
**與珍珠是兩味藥**：珍珠 Margarita（珠，0.3–1g，多研末）vs 珍珠母 Margaritiferae Concha usta（煅貝殼，21–30g，打碎先煎）。用量差 30 倍，調劑錯了是實質風險。
cautions_en: The coursework lists no contraindications or cautions for Zhen Zhu Mu; this card does not supply any. Zhen Zhu Mu's own entry (Materia Medica Abbbreviated.md) likewise lists none — it was only used to fill nature/flavor, channels, actions, and dosage.

**Zhen Zhu and Zhen Zhu Mu are two different materials**: Zhen Zhu is Margarita (the pearl, 0.3–1 g, usually powdered) and Zhen Zhu Mu is Margaritiferae Concha usta (the calcined shell, 21–30 g, crushed and pre-decocted). The doses differ roughly thirtyfold, so a dispensing error here carries real risk.

cautions_zh: 脾胃虛寒者慎用。
cautions_en: Use with caution in Spleen-Stomach Deficiency Cold.

contraindications_zh: **不安全、已廢用**：課件紫雪丹卡明寫「AD lists historically and calls it generally the incorrect herb; Aristolochia is unsafe/obsolete」，§17 毒性段重複同一警語。
正確用藥為木香（Rx. Aucklandiae）——課件明指「AD identifies this as the proper herb」。
contraindications_en: **Unsafe and obsolete**: the Zi Xue Dan card states that American Dragon lists it historically and calls it generally the incorrect herb, and that Aristolochia is unsafe/obsolete; the toxicity section repeats the same warning.
The correct herb is Mu Xiang (Rx. Aucklandiae) — the coursework states American Dragon identifies this as the proper herb.

contraindications_zh: 本品為馬兜鈴科植物，含馬兜鈴酸，具腎毒性與致癌性；《中華人民共和國藥典》2005年版起已取消收載，臨床禁用，處方中以土木香或木香替代。
contraindications_en: Aristolochia species containing aristolochic acid (nephrotoxic, carcinogenic); removed from the Chinese Pharmacopoeia since the 2005 edition; do not use clinically — substitute Tu Mu Xiang or Mu Xiang.

data/pathology/condition_canon_shortlist.branch_value: Lumbar disc degeneration is rooted in kidney deficiency — the kidney governs bone and generates marrow, so kidney-qi deficiency leaves the lower back undernourished and the disc poorly anchored. Prolonged sitting, repetitive strain, or a fall/twist injury then produces qi stagnation and blood stasis obstructing the channels. If wind-cold-damp invades on top of this, channel qi and blood become further obstructed, intensifying pain that radiates down the leg along the Bladder and Gallbladder channel pathways — presenting as combined low-back-and-leg pain (腰腿痛). The root is kidney deficiency; cold-damp or blood stasis is the manifestation, so treatment must distinguish root from branch and their urgency to decide the order of dispelling pathogens versus tonifying the kidney.
data/pathology/condition_canon_shortlist.main_value:
Low back pain has troubled the Chinese people for thousands of years; in the Huangdi Neijing (Yellow Emperor's Inner Classic) it is called "lumbar-spine pain" or "lumbar pain."

Ancient texts contain many vivid descriptions of low back pain, for example: "broken waist," "broken spine," "spinal pain as if the lumbar region were snapping," "lumbar pain preventing bending forward or backward," "lumbar pain radiating to the shoulder," "lumbar pain along both sides of the spine reaching up to the head with heaviness," "lumbar pain radiating to the lower abdomen," "lumbar and back pain with aching of the lower legs," and so on.

Later generations of physicians divided low back pain into "sudden lumbar pain" (acute low back pain) and "chronic lumbar pain." The experience of the ancients resembles that of modern people: daily physical labor, prolonged fixed postures (such as prolonged sitting, prolonged standing, or bending), muscular strain, and acute lumbar sprain (traumatic injury) all produce low back pain.

Analyzed by pattern identification, low back pain is mainly differentiated into the following types:

1. External invasion of the six pathogenic factors (Wind, Cold, Dampness)

As early as the Han-dynasty Shanghan Lun (Treatise on Cold Damage), it was recognized that during a common cold, external Wind-Cold pathogens invading the body produce "Taiyang-stage disease," which first affects the Bladder meridian and the Du (Governing) Vessel. These two channels influence the entire back, and the region of pain overlaps with the low back.

Simply put, this is low back pain occurring with a cold, so it is accompanied by other symptoms such as headache, neck pain, shoulder and upper back pain, pain in the buttocks, thighs, calves, and back of the knees, generalized joint pain, fever, aversion to cold, absence or presence of sweating, a thin white tongue coating, and a floating, tight pulse.

External "Dampness" also readily causes low back pain; it tends to invade the Gallbladder meridian and the Dai (Girdle) Vessel at the waist, worsening whenever the weather turns cold or rainy, or during autumn and winter.

If this Wind-Cold-Damp painful obstruction (Bi) accumulates for many years without being cured, it is often accompanied by heat, swelling, and pain of the joints throughout the body. The pain and stiffness resemble modern rheumatoid arthritis.

When a person is invaded by external "Cold-Damp" pathogens, Spleen-Stomach dysfunction also arises, reflected on the back near the Back-Shu points of the Spleen (BL-20) and Stomach (BL-21), and in turn affecting the Dai Vessel at the waist, producing coldness and a heavy, dragging sensation in the lumbar region and below. This is what the ancients called the "Shen Zhuo" (Kidney Fixity) pattern.

Because low back pain occurs so frequently, it is easy to verify. Observation of many members has shown that whenever the three leg Yang meridians (Gallbladder, Stomach, and Bladder) together with the Kidney meridian present Deficiency patterns (see figure below), it is almost impossible to escape the grip of low back pain, with the probability especially high after entering autumn and winter.

The meridian pattern most prone to low back pain

Starting around 2020, a member, Mr. C, developed low back pain every year in late autumn and early winter. Continuous observation through 2022 showed that at this time each year his Gallbladder and Stomach meridians began to show Deficiency patterns, confirming the phenomenon that external Cold depletes the energy of the Yang meridians.

However, low back pain can still occur in the hottest part of summer. During the extremely hot "sanfu" period of July–August 2022, a female member, Ms. B, reported that one morning she suddenly had low back pain so severe she could not stand up. Her meridian assessment is shown below; comparing this meridian chart with the pattern most prone to low back pain described above, they are nearly identical.

Severe low back and upper back pain during the hottest summer of 2022

This typically occurs in people with a "Cold-type Yang-Deficient meridian constitution." After entering the hot summer, the energy of the Gallbladder, Stomach, and Kidney meridians remains at winter levels without a corresponding rise; combined with a Bladder meridian Deficiency pattern, the entire back's meridian Qi and Blood become insufficient, and low back pain naturally follows.[@ad:1]

2. Spleen-Stomach dysfunction with internal retention of Water-Rheum

As mentioned above, external Cold can affect the lumbar region and cause cold-type pain. In addition, when a person frequently stays up late and the Spleen-Stomach's capacity to generate Qi and Blood declines, impaired transformation and transportation of body fluids can also produce low back pain.

This is because Chinese medicine holds that the Spleen governs transformation and transportation, chiefly of the body's water. When water metabolism is impaired, Phlegm-Rheum forms within the body.

This is reflected at the Back-Shu points of the Spleen, Stomach, Kidney, and Bladder on the back, and is likewise a major cause of low back pain.

In addition, symptoms such as generalized or limb edema, cough, wheezing, dizziness, shortness of breath with weak speech, dry mouth and thirst, chest pain, and so on readily appear.

This meridian presentation of internally retained Water-Rheum is most commonly seen in the "Iron Triangle" meridian pattern and the "Inverted Iron Triangle" meridian pattern, which are discussed in many articles.

Because the so-called "Iron Triangle" meridian pattern appears readily during summer, this pattern features severe Deficiency of the Spleen meridian.

One member caught a cold in July 2022 and developed low back pain, flank pain, and related cold symptoms. The meridian chart from that day is shared below:

Low back pain during a summer cold in 2022

3. Deficiency-Cold of the abdomen

The low back pain caused by abdominal Deficiency-Cold described above can occur not only in winter but also quite readily in the hot summer; the key lies in drinking iced water and consuming cold-natured foods.

This meridian phenomenon can be clearly observed through changes in the energy of the three hand Yang meridians.

Take one member as an example: in early 2022, while it was still winter, he developed severe low back pain one day, with all-day fatigue and drowsiness yet disturbed sleep, gastric bloating, indigestion, sore throat, and nasal discharge — symptoms much like a cold, but in fact a manifestation of internal Deficiency-Cold. The meridian chart from that day is shown below:

Low back pain can also appear when the three hand Yang meridians show Deficiency patterns

4. Kidney Deficiency (Qi Deficiency, Yang Deficiency, Yin Deficiency) and Liver-Kidney insufficiency

Because Asians have long been steeped in Chinese medicine, many people, on hearing of a sore lower back, will tease that it is "Kidney Deficiency."

This is because Chinese medicine holds that "the lumbar region is the mansion of the Kidney," so low back pain is closely bound to the Kidney of Chinese medicine — not the anatomical kidney of Western medicine, but "Kidney Qi," "Kidney Yin," and "Kidney Yang."

When Water-Rheum is retained internally for a long time, kidney disease can develop; sexual excess, overexertion, or the decline of Kidney Qi with aging produces low back pain. Low back pain is reflected at the Back-Shu points, chiefly in the region of the Kidney Shu (BL-23) and Sanjiao Shu (BL-22).

Besides the Kidney, the Liver is also closely related to low back pain, because Chinese medicine holds that "the Liver governs the sinews and the Kidney governs the bones."

Only when Liver Blood is abundant can the sinews be nourished and free of aching pain. The Kidney governs skeletal growth and repair; when Liver and Kidney are weak, lumbar soreness and pain also occur.

On this basis, for the past thousand years Chinese medicine has held that chronic musculoskeletal diseases are mainly caused by the decline of Liver and Kidney Qi and Blood, which is why the middle-aged and elderly can hardly avoid them.

Accordingly, there is a variant of the Iron Triangle meridian pattern (see figure below) that is most prone to produce long-standing low back pain. This pattern appears most readily after middle age, which is why many middle-aged people suffer chronic low back pain.

The meridian pattern most prone to chronic low back pain

5. Damp-Heat in the Lower Jiao

Almost everything discussed above relates to Wind, Cold, and Dampness, because the ancients considered these three factors most relevant to low back pain. However, "Heat" can in fact also cause low back pain, and this readily occurs in summer.

When a person has Damp-Heat in the Lower Jiao, the lumbar region is also affected. In Chinese medicine the Lower Jiao refers to the large intestine, small intestine, and bladder. Low back pain reflected at the Back-Shu points here also includes the regions of the Large Intestine Shu (BL-25), Small Intestine Shu (BL-27), and Bladder Shu (BL-28).

Consequently, this type of low back pain is accompanied by abnormal symptoms of the intestines and bladder, such as loose, foul-smelling stools, burning pain on urination or urinary difficulty, lower-abdominal distension and pain, yellowish-white foul-smelling vaginal discharge, thirst and dry mouth, and a red tongue with a yellow, greasy coating.

This meridian pattern is commonly seen in summer as Excess patterns of the Shaoyang meridians (Sanjiao and Gallbladder) and the Yangming meridians (Large Intestine and Stomach). Up to 2022, some members have reported that this extremely hot meridian pattern can indeed also produce low back pain and lumbar soreness.

For low back pain occurring in any season, the method of improvement is actually simple: regularly pat and tap the thigh portions of the Gallbladder, Stomach, and Bladder meridians; use massage and tuina to knead apart muscular adhesions along these meridians; keep the abdomen warm; and take hot half-body baths. These measures can bring rapid improvement and recovery in almost all cases.

In November 2020, Cloud TCM published a successful case of improving autumn-winter low back pain; most people who follow the procedure improve.[@post:208]

When this individual was interviewed again in January 2022, he said that although the winter of 2022 was very cold, he no longer had any low back pain — evidence that meridian patting is genuinely effective for improving low back pain, with little tendency to recur.

Modern medicine has an extremely thorough understanding of low back pain. The causes of lumbar pain (low back pain) are very numerous and can be described as highly complex, because it is a symptom common to many diseases. The common causes of low back pain listed below can be divided into the following three categories:

1. Mechanical low back pain: The two types below are the most common; this kind of low back pain generally falls within the scope of physical therapy and rehabilitation medicine.

Muscle, tendon, and ligament strain: This is the cause of the majority of lumbar and low back pain. Pain arises when the lower back is used improperly or overused, and it usually resolves with adequate rest alone.

Spinal abnormalities: When low back pain is accompanied by symptoms such as lower-limb pain, numbness, or weakness, disc herniation is very likely. Other possibilities include: intervertebral disc degeneration, lumbar spondylolisthesis, spondylolysis, spinal nerve root compression, vertebral fracture, foraminal stenosis, compression fractures caused by osteoporosis, and so on.

Degenerative disc herniation is one cause of low back pain.

2. Non-mechanical low back pain: The conditions below are the most common; these should be evaluated by oncology, urology, hepatobiliary and gastroenterology, rheumatology and immunology, infectious disease, and related specialties.

Urinary system diseases: Renal inflammation, calculi, and tumors can cause low back pain, including acute pyelonephritis, urinary tract stones, kidney stones, renal tumors, and renal obstruction.

Reproductive system diseases: In women, uterine fibroids, ovarian tumors, and pelvic inflammatory disease; in men, varicocele, testicular torsion, and orchitis or epididymitis may also present with low back pain.

Digestive system diseases: The pain of gallstones with cholecystitis may radiate from the right upper abdomen to the right posterior flank. Pancreatitis may also cause left-sided flank pain.

Immune system diseases: Ankylosing spondylitis, rheumatoid arthritis, and viral infections can all cause severe low back pain.

3. Referred pain: This refers to pain that does not originate in the lower back but is referred from elsewhere. The two most common are:

Piriformis syndrome: Some people have pain in the lower back, buttock, and hip joint without any disc herniation; it is instead caused by an abnormality of the piriformis muscle in the buttock, and is commonly seen in sciatica.

Hip labral tear: A tear of the cartilage that surrounds and stabilizes the acetabulum, producing pain with movement.

Anterior pelvic tilt: Caused by prolonged sitting and imbalance of the lumbar musculature, anterior pelvic tilt is a precursor factor in almost all low back pain.

Pain in the buttock or other regions can also be referred to the lower back.

The causes of low back pain discussed above can be considered quite comprehensive. Nevertheless, in a certain proportion of people, low back pain may not belong to any of the above categories: the cause remains unidentified and no organic lesion is present. In such cases, it is well suited to exploration through the meridian theory of Traditional Chinese Medicine.
