Pain in the joints of the limbs is called 'arthritis' in modern medicine, referring to any disease that affects the joints. The common symptoms are 'joint pain' and 'stiffness'; other symptoms that may appear together with them include: redness, warmth, swelling, and reduced range of motion of the affected joint.

There are many types of arthritis. The most common is 'degenerative arthritis (osteoarthritis)': with advancing age, the synovial fluid within the joint capsule gradually decreases, and after the cartilage inside the joint wears down and cracks, various kinds of pain are produced. It commonly appears in the knees, hips, neck, and ankles, or in the frequently used joints of the hands and feet, with a higher incidence in women.

'Rheumatoid arthritis' is an autoimmune disease in which immune cells and antibodies attack the joints and produce an inflammatory response. It most often invades the hands, leading to finger deformity, and affects more women than men. Because it is a disease of the immune system, the related diseases arising as complications are numerous.

'Gout' is also a common type of arthritis, caused by urate crystals depositing within the joint, producing an inflammatory response of redness, swelling, heat, and pain; it affects more men than women. Other arthritides — such as ankylosing spondylitis, systemic lupus erythematosus, fibromyalgia, septic arthritis, and so on — make the typology quite complex.

Arthritis can also be a symptom of other diseases, for example: psoriasis (psoriatic arthritis), reactive arthritis, hepatitis, Lyme disease, Sjogren's syndrome, Hashimoto's thyroiditis, celiac disease, inflammatory bowel disease, Henoch-Schonlein purpura, and so on.

Modern medicine has found that the causes of arthritis are many, chiefly aging, overuse injury (sports injury), heredity, an excessively rich diet, obesity, immune system dysregulation, hyperlipidemia, alcohol addiction, medication side effects, and so on.

Modern medical treatments for arthritis, apart from physical therapy, mainly involve the use of 'corticosteroids,' non-steroidal analgesic anti-inflammatory drugs, hyaluronic acid injections, surgical operations, and so on.

In recent times, very many health supplements have been found to improve arthritis — for example glucosamine, collagen, fish oil, methylsulfonylmethane (MSM), turmeric, and so on. These are quite popular and used by very many people, and they clearly belong to the category of alternative therapies.

Chinese medicine is also a form of alternative therapy. If one can incorporate the TCM concepts of the 'meridians,' 'Zang-Fu Qi and Blood,' and 'Cold and Heat,' it can likewise serve as a good adjunctive approach to improvement.

Epigastric discomfort has definitely troubled the Chinese people for over a thousand years. In ancient times it was called 'Cao Za (gnawing distress)' or 'Xin Cao (heart gnawing),' a common symptom referring to a feeling of discomfort in the epigastric region.

The core sensation of 'Cao Za' is an indescribable discomfort in the epigastrium (the pit of the stomach) — neither pain nor distension, but something resembling a feeling of hunger, a burning sensation, a churning sensation, or a feeling of emptiness, possibly accompanied by belching and acid regurgitation.

The ancient text Lei Zheng Zhi Cai (Tailored Treatments by Pattern Classification) describes it: 'The Cao condition belongs to the Stomach; it is commonly called heart-gnawing, but that is wrong. Its manifestation seems like hunger yet is not hunger, seems like pain yet is not pain, with anguished unease in the epigastrium. It may be accompanied by belching, glomus, and oppression, gradually reaching acid swallowing and fluid retention, with hidden pain in front of the chest.'

In modern medicine, this sensation is most commonly seen in gastroesophageal reflux disease, functional dyspepsia, chronic gastritis, or peptic ulcer, and in emotion-related disorders such as anxiety disorder, depression, and so on.

Ancient Chinese medicine long ago recognized that 'Cao Za' is related to the emotions (worry-pensiveness, anger). Modern medicine has also confirmed that the brain and gut are tightly connected through the 'brain-gut axis.' Anxiety and stress markedly aggravate gastric sensations, leading to 'heart gnawing' without any organic problem — a situation often called 'gastric neurosis.'

Pathological basis: dysfunction of the central nervous system affects the gastrointestinal nervous system, leading to abnormal sensory and motor function.

This can be considered a syndrome, comprising symptoms such as belching, acid swallowing, nausea, dry retching, epigastric glomus (Xin Xia Pi), epigastric pain, and so on appearing together. From the perspective of the meridians and Zang-Fu organs, it can be divided mainly into the following types:

1. Liver-Spleen disharmony; Liver-Stomach disharmony

'Liver-Spleen disharmony' and 'Liver-Stomach disharmony' are the main causes of virtually all Spleen-Stomach discomfort, mostly arising from 'emotional depression' or 'irregular daily living,' producing Liver constraint, Liver Qi invading the Stomach transversely, and a series of symptoms of Spleen-Stomach weakness.

This is because, based on Five-Phase theory, the Liver belongs to 'Wood' and the Spleen-Stomach to 'Earth'; when Wood overcontrols Earth, the patterns of 'Liver-Spleen disharmony' and 'Liver-Stomach disharmony' naturally appear. These symptoms therefore occur in all four seasons and are entirely within one's own control.

The Liver governs upward effusion and can regulate the Qi dynamic of the whole body. The Spleen governs transportation and transformation; the Stomach governs intake and digestion, being the sea of water and grain. The middle burner generates Qi and Blood, which nourish the Liver; when the Liver is nourished, its coursing and discharge remain measured.

If Liver disease invades the Spleen and Stomach, there will be hiccup, belching, acid swallowing, nausea and vomiting, indigestion, abdominal distension and pain, and restlessness with quickness to anger — thereby affecting the postnatal generation of Qi and Blood.

Those who have studied Chinese medicine have seen these abstract theories thousands upon thousands of times, yet they remain abstract text. Now, using data and charts, this phenomenon can be clearly seen with the eyes and verified.

When a person's meridians present a Liver meridian Excess pattern, the Spleen meridian very readily shows Deficiency, verifying that the abstract Five-Phase 'Wood overcontrolling Earth' exists.

From the figure below it can be clearly seen that in the spring and summer seasons, Liver meridian energy is even more exuberant, so the Spleen meridian is even weaker. As soon as the weather turns hot, the Spleen and Stomach feel unwell — this is what causes it.

When the Liver meridian is Excess, the Spleen meridian readily shows Deficiency.

In meridian terms, moreover, the Liver meridian 'skirts the Stomach, belongs to the Liver, and nets the Gallbladder'; therefore, whether or not the Liver meridian is unobstructed directly affects the harmonious descent of Stomach Qi. The harmonious descent of Stomach Qi must depend on the Liver's upward-effusing, dispersing, and discharging Qi, and normal discharging function in turn requires an open and relaxed heart and chest.

When the Liver meridian is Excess, the Stomach meridian also frequently shows Excess together with it — this is the classic phenomenon of 'Liver-Stomach disharmony.' The interaction between the Liver and Stomach meridians is also influenced by the weather, being more pronounced after entering spring and summer, with another peak appearing in winter.

When the Liver meridian is Excess, the Stomach meridian also frequently shows Excess together with it.

According to the long-term observation of Cloud TCM members, although the two meridian phenomena above appear to manifest physically according to season, at any time whatsoever, merely staying up late or suffering insomnia for more than 3 consecutive days lets one clearly see one's own Liver meridian Excess, Spleen meridian Deficiency, and Stomach meridian Excess — this is not affected by season.

In 2025, from several thousand sets of meridian data on stomach discomfort, Cloud TCM could truly and clearly discern this meridian phenomenon of Liver-plus-Stomach-meridian Excess with Spleen meridian Deficiency — that is, the Iron Triangle meridian pattern.

The most common meridian pattern when the stomach feels unwell.

In January 2022, a member living in Malaysia reported that in the morning he kept retching, his abdomen had been bloated for half the day, with dizziness, weak limbs, and no desire to do anything — precisely the Iron Triangle meridian pattern.

It suddenly occurred to him to resolve it with 'Bagua ear therapy' plus 'acupuncture.' For the first time in his life, he needled the Hegu, Zusanli, and Taichong points of the Large Intestine, Stomach, and Liver meridians on his own body. After pressing and needling, turbid Qi kept discharging both upward and downward, the dizziness stopped, and he felt extremely comfortable — he had successfully resolved his own health crisis.

Since Liver Qi constrained in the body for a long time readily brews and transforms into Fire, and the Fire-Heat Qi then goes on to overcontrol the Spleen and Stomach, it can be called a vicious cycle: poor emotions and lifestyle habits are quite evidently the source of a myriad diseases!

2. Yangming Stomach Heat

From the Liver and Stomach meridian Excess phenomena above, the phenomenon of Liver Fire and Stomach Fire flaring together is clearly visible. Chinese medicine speaks of a 'Yangming Heat pattern,' where the so-called 'Yangming' refers to the Large Intestine and Stomach meridians. As far back as the Han dynasty, the Shang Han Lun described Yangming disease — the phenomenon of stomach discomfort caused by Stomach Heat.

In stomach discomfort caused by Stomach Heat, the stomach has a distinctly pungent-hot sensation, or frequent sour-hot feelings, accompanied by bad breath, gastric acid or regurgitation of sour fluid, constipation, a yellow tongue coating, and a surging or slippery pulse.

At this point, simply clearing the Stomach Fire makes this sensation disappear. The 'San Huang Xie Xin Tang (Three-Yellow Heart-Draining Decoction)' mentioned in the Shang Han Lun works very well. Cloud TCM member Mr. A shared that whenever he feels bad breath, dry mouth, and an odd feeling in the stomach, taking 'San Huang Xie Xin Tang' just once improves it by more than half — it truly is caused by Stomach Fire.

The Fire-draining herbs of Chinese medicine are very numerous. Taking 'Zuo Jin Wan (Left Metal Pill)' as an example: although it has only two ingredients, its effect is surprisingly good — simple in composition yet concentrated in power. Because Chinese herbs drain Stomach Fire very quickly, one must stop as soon as the disease is checked; they cannot be taken long-term. If the gastrointestinal discomfort is chronic, then it is not merely Stomach Fire.

In the phenomenon of Liver-Stomach disharmony, the disease originates in the Liver and develops secondarily in the Stomach. Thus, although there are symptoms of stomach discomfort, Liver meridian symptoms (hypochondriac pain, chest oppression, wiry pulse) appear first, and the Stomach meridian symptoms appear afterward. So the real killer is the 'Liver,' and treatment can also begin directly from the Liver — 'Xiao Chai Hu Tang (Minor Bupleurum Decoction)' or 'Si Ni San (Frigid Extremities Powder)' is a good starting point.[@ad:1]

3. Stomach Deficiency-Cold

The Stomach Heat mentioned above actually appears with a probability of only about 26%. The Huangdi Neijing states that Yangming is normally 'abundant in Qi and abundant in Blood,' so in theory Yangming meridian energy should usually be robust.

However, from large volumes of meridian data on modern people, modern people's Large Intestine meridian energy is very robust, while Stomach meridian energy is generally weak, with a rather low probability of showing Excess — evidently most people's Stomach meridian energy is weak, and their stomach is Deficient-Cold.

The Large Intestine meridian shows Excess with high probability, while the probability of Stomach meridian Excess is rather low.

Discomfort caused by Stomach Deficiency-Cold brings a sour taste in the mouth accompanied by epigastric pain, worse when the weather turns cold or after eating cold-natured foods, while hot food and drink relieve it instead; abdominal bloating, poor appetite, weak limbs, shortness of breath, a pale complexion, a pale tongue, and a thin pulse.

People of the 'Cold-type Yang-Deficient meridian constitution' are usually extremely sensitive to the temperature of the weather. During late October 2025, a member on a business trip to Japan felt the temperature plunge and felt very unwell in the stomach.

From his usual meridian phenomena — Gallbladder and Stomach meridian Deficiency, which worsens when the temperature drops sharply — simply checking the weather forecast allowed him to estimate that Spleen-Stomach trouble would appear during his business trip to Japan.

A temperature drop on a business trip, with sudden stomach discomfort.

Since this is Stomach Cold, one need only take hot-natured medicinals to warm the stomach to obtain improvement; on this basis, 'Li Zhong Tang (Regulate the Middle Decoction),' 'An Zhong San (Calm the Middle Powder),' or 'Wu Zhu Yu Tang (Evodia Decoction)' suits the constitution of modern people very well.

Quite a few Cloud TCM members have used Li Zhong Tang to improve their own Spleen-Stomach Deficiency-Cold, accumulating very many real cases. Since this Chinese herbal formula is easy to obtain, everyone can verify it for themselves.

Besides Chinese herbs, physical therapy also works: this member afterward continuously soaked his lower body in Japanese hot springs, and indeed achieved an improvement effect.

4. Mixed Cold and Heat

Beyond the Stomach Heat and Stomach Cold above, there is a type of person who has both Stomach Heat and Stomach Cold — this is the phenomenon of Cold and Heat mixed within the body. At this point, Chinese herbal formulas that are simultaneously hot and cold in nature can be used for improvement.

The typical symptom of this simultaneous Heat and Cold affecting the Spleen and Stomach is the Pi (glomus) pattern mentioned in Chinese medicine — namely 'Xin Xia Pi (epigastric glomus),' the phenomenon of discomfort in the epigastric region.

As far back as the Han dynasty, the Shang Han Lun stated: 'Fullness without pain — this is Pi (glomus).' 'Ban Xia Xie Xin Tang (Pinellia Heart-Draining Decoction)' can be used for improvement, with very rapid and good results.

Summarizing the above: if meridian examination shows the three Hand Yang meridians in Excess and the three Foot Yang meridians in Deficiency — especially the Shaoyang and Yangming meridians — this epigastric-glomus symptom appears most readily; everyone can verify this for themselves.

The meridian phenomenon of Cold and Heat mixed within the body.

5. Food damage

Every year during the Lunar New Year holidays, Spleen-Stomach discomfort readily appears, and the reason is simple: eating too much!

In ancient times, this phenomenon was called 'Shang Shi (food damage)' — improper diet damaging the Spleen and Stomach and causing indigestion — most often improved with 'Bao He Wan (Preserve Harmony Pill).' In modern times there are also many similar medications that can improve this phenomenon, so taking Chinese herbs is not strictly necessary.

When encountering Spleen-Stomach discomfort, besides identifying causes such as Stomach Heat, Stomach Cold, and mixed Cold-Heat, improving lifestyle habits and emotions is the true foundation. Combined with patting and massaging the relevant meridians and acupoints, improvement can be achieved within a very short time.

Epigastric pain has absolutely troubled the Chinese people for over a thousand years, and the location of the pain is consistent with stomach pain as defined by modern medicine.

The Huangdi Neijing already mentioned 'pain at the stomach cavity, at the heart' (Wei Wan Dang Xin Er Tong), so later generations also called it 'heart-abdomen pain' or 'heart-stomach pain.'

'Heart' is mentioned because the heart pain and pain below the heart referred to in ancient literature also included epigastric pain; the ancients therefore often discussed stomach pain and heart pain together in a combined manner, and even held that heart disease is in fact caused by obstruction of Qi and Blood in the meridians near the epigastrium.

The ancients' classification of the causes of stomach pain is very complex — for example: Deficiency pain, Qi pain, Heat pain, Cold pain, stasis pain, food pain, worm pain, and the pain below the heart of the major Jie Xiong (chest-bind) pattern; both 'externally contracted Cold Damage' and 'internal damage from miscellaneous diseases' can produce stomach pain.

From the meridian perspective, stomach pain is also very complex, because the meridians leading to the abdomen include: the Conception Vessel (Ren Mai), Penetrating Vessel (Chong Mai), Spleen meridian, Liver meridian, Stomach meridian, Gallbladder meridian, and Kidney meridian.

Moreover, all the meridians of the hand ultimately lead to the abdomen as well, so exploring the causes of stomach pain from the meridians can also be very complex.

Setting aside these complex factors, from observation of large volumes of modern meridian data combined with members' actual reports, it has been found that the causes of stomach pain can be reduced to two main types: one is a stomach that is too Hot, the other a stomach that is too Cold. They are described separately below:

1. The stomach is too Hot

Modern medicine finds that some people, because of heavy stress and poor sleep, frequently develop symptoms such as palpitations, chest oppression, and stomach pain; they visit cardiology and gastroenterology, ultrasound examinations find no problem, and they are finally referred to psychosomatic medicine and defined as having 'autonomic nervous system dysregulation.'

This phenomenon is in fact consistent with what Chinese medicine calls 'Liver Qi constraint' and 'Liver Fire invading the Stomach.' When a person is under heavy stress and in a depressed mood, Liver Qi invades the Stomach: the epigastrium becomes distended, full, and painful, with hypochondriac pain, chest oppression, poor appetite, bitter taste in the mouth, dry mouth, belching, gastric acid or vomiting, unsmooth bowel movements, a thin white or thin yellow tongue coating, and a wiry pulse.

This is quite a common presentation — one could say most TCM clinics treat this pattern every day — and meridian examination can completely confirm this phenomenon.

Anyone under heavy stress who sleeps poorly at night will, after several consecutive days, display the phenomenon of 'Stomach meridian Excess' shown in the figure below. This can also be called the meridian pattern of autonomic dysregulation, and it very readily produces stomach pain!

The meridian pattern commonly seen in Fire-Heat type epigastric pain.

From the figure above, one can see Stomach meridian Excess with concurrent Liver meridian Excess, representing excessive energy, while Spleen meridian Deficiency represents weak Spleen Qi. This extremely unbalanced phenomenon very readily produces a series of gastrointestinal complaints (stomach pain, bloating, indigestion, and so on).

In addition, this meridian pattern also very readily appears naturally under the influence of the weather each year after entering April-May, so in summer, Fire-Heat type epigastric pain readily appears.

This is actually very easy to understand: when both the Liver and Stomach meridians of a person's body are in Excess, one can also say that Liver Fire is affecting Stomach Fire, so Fire-Heat type epigastric pain appears.

If this meridian pattern is combined with the Fire-transforming phenomenon of Triple Burner and Large Intestine meridian Excess, the body's underlying Fire is even more exuberant; at this point, Chinese herbs based on 'Huang Lian (Coptis)' and 'Huang Qin (Scutellaria)' can usually be used to bring the Fire down quickly.

Some people develop the so-called 'Xin Xia Pi (epigastric glomus)' pattern, in which pain appears specifically around the epigastrium; taking 'Ban Xia Xie Xin Tang (Pinellia Heart-Draining Decoction)' brings rapid improvement.

2. The stomach is too Cold

Stomach meridian Excess causes stomach pain, but Deficiency also causes stomach pain — in that case it is the opposite, caused by the stomach being 'too Cold.'

Modern medicine finds that winter is the season in which gastrointestinal diseases appear with high frequency; many patients with chronic gastritis and gastrointestinal ulcers readily relapse and develop stomach pain, and meridian examination can completely confirm this phenomenon.

Traditional Chinese medicine says that 'Spleen-Stomach Deficiency-Cold' predisposes to stomach pain. From the figure below it can be clearly seen that usually, when the Stomach meridian is Deficient, the Gallbladder meridian is also Deficient, and Deficiency also appears in tandem in the Triple Burner, Large Intestine, Kidney, and Liver meridians (see figure below).

In Yin-Cold type epigastric pain, Gallbladder and Stomach meridian Deficiency can be seen.

Stomach pain caused by this 'Cold pathogen invading the Stomach' improves as soon as the abdomen is warmed and becomes more painful after eating cold food; the body shows aversion to cold, vomiting of clear froth, absence of thirst with a preference for drinking hot water, a white tongue coating, and a tight pulse.

In stomach disease of a long-standing 'Spleen-Stomach Deficiency-Cold' constitution, besides dull, lingering epigastric pain, there may also be poor appetite, regurgitation of clear fluid, pain worse when hungry, ice-cold limbs, loose thin stools, and clear, copious urine — chronic and unresolving for years, very difficult to cure at the root.

Chinese medicine constantly says not to consume cold-natured foods or iced water long-term; simply observe for a period of time, and the relationship between stomach pain and cold-natured foods can be discovered.

During April 2025, a member shared that starting that month he had become obsessed with drinking cassia seed (Jue Ming Zi) tea, nearly a large jug every day. At first he felt nothing; gradually, he found that he was actually beginning to develop stomach pain.

One night, he was awakened in his sleep by epigastric pain. He guessed this might be caused by his abdomen being too Cold, so he immediately took 'Fu Zi Li Zhong Tang (Aconite Regulate-the-Middle Decoction),' a hot-natured medicine — and unexpectedly, it eased within a few minutes.

This is classic epigastric pain caused by abdominal Yin-Cold: although the energy of his Stomach meridian was quite strong, with long-term intake of cold-natured Chinese herbs or foods, the stomach still could not withstand it.

Whether the Stomach meridian is Excess or Deficient, over a long time the so-called 'Stomach Yin Deficiency' readily appears, with chronic stomach pain — dull, hidden pain, dry mouth and tongue, easy hunger yet inability to eat, dry retching, hiccup, regurgitation, dry stools, and a red tongue with scant fluids, little or no coating, and a wiry-thin or somewhat rapid pulse.

This is the result of long-standing stomach disease damaging Yin-Blood, or of excessive internal Heat consuming Stomach Yin.

In addition, the ancients also found that eating too much causes 'food accumulation and stagnation,' which likewise causes stomach pain; it can be resolved with digestive, enzyme-type Chinese herbs, being caused by brief dietary excess.

There is a type of person in whom trauma or various other causes produce obstruction of Qi and Blood in the abdominal meridians and stomach pain; the location of this stomach pain is fixed and unchanging. Simply taking some Blood-activating, stasis-transforming medicinals, or kneading open the blockage point with massage, suffices to cure it.

Therefore, differentiating stomach pain from the TCM angle is actually easy — one need only judge whether it is Cold or Heat. Usually in summer, as long as one has not drunk too much iced water, it is Heat; in winter, it is usually Cold.

For Heat-type stomach pain, the effect of taking cold-cool herbs is very fast. The simplest way to treat neurasthenia is to slow down, stay away from computers and mobile phones, and let the brain rest completely. Since the ancient Chinese had no modern technology, their probability of developing this illness must have been very low.

To understand the true cause of neurasthenia, the simplest and most direct method is to find a person with neurasthenia and test their meridians over the long term; one can then know which meridian abnormalities are responsible.

Because a great many members have reported being troubled by neurasthenia over the past several years, summarizing these meridian patterns reveals some of the principal underlying causes, chiefly the following:

1. Liver Qi stagnation, Heart-Spleen dual Deficiency, Heart Blood Deficiency

Traditional Chinese medicine holds that "the Heart governs the Blood and vessels." When a person overthinks, Heart Blood is consumed and damaged, leading to insufficiency of Heart Blood, with symptoms such as palpitations, insomnia, excessive dreaming, being easily startled, forgetfulness, and dizziness.

When the Heart's Spirit functions are disturbed, this may manifest as restlessness of the Heart Spirit, mental abstraction, sadness with a desire to weep, inability to control one's emotions, inner agitation, unquiet sleep, and repeated yawning; in severe cases even speech abnormalities may appear.

The ancients called this symptom picture "visceral agitation (zang zao)," which somewhat resembles what is now called neurasthenia; Gan Mai Dazao Tang (Licorice, Wheat and Jujube Decoction) is used to improve it.

The ancients held that "pensiveness damages the Spleen": excessive thinking not only damages the Heart's Blood but also affects the functions of the Spleen and Stomach — the body's essential source for generating Qi and Blood. When both are impaired, the Spirit cannot be stabilized.

The ancients held that "pensiveness damages the Spleen" — excessive thinking harms the Spleen and Stomach.

Chinese medicine also holds that "the Liver governs the Qi of the whole body," directing the movement of all Qi within the human body. Liver Qi must remain unimpeded and free-flowing; when it becomes "constrained and stagnant," the seven emotions (joy, anger, worry, pensiveness, sadness, fear, fright) cannot be regulated smoothly — thus Liver Qi stagnation can also produce neurasthenia.

If this constrained Liver Qi accumulates in the body for a period of time, a "transformation into Fire" occurs, at which point the neurasthenia becomes even more severe.

All of the above descriptions can be verified through meridian testing. From large numbers of neurasthenia meridian patterns, there is a relatively high probability of finding "the extreme form of the Iron Triangle meridian pattern." (Open to read for deeper understanding.)

In this meridian pattern there are Spleen Deficiency with Stomach Excess, Liver-Stomach disharmony, Liver-Spleen disharmony, and Heart-Spleen dual Deficiency, together with Deficiency of the Heart and Pericardium meridians. The Shaoyang and Yangming meridians are in Excess, so the interior of the body is very hot.

A certain proportion of people display this meridian pattern in all four seasons; it is a meridian model extremely prone to neurasthenia.

The extreme form of the Iron Triangle meridian pattern.

In this meridian pattern especially, the Bladder meridian and Kidney meridian are Deficient virtually year-round. The Bladder meridian and the Governing Vessel (Du Mai) engage the central nervous system, and the Kidney is closely related to the brain; excessive energy consumption may well be the chief cause of the neurasthenia.

When the Qi and Blood of the Bladder meridian and Governing Vessel are insufficient, neurasthenia readily appears.

In 2024 a member shared that the saying "pensiveness damages the Spleen" was something he could completely understand: whenever he spent a stretch of time intensely programming, he would develop stomach bloating and indigestion, and eventually a genuine feeling of neurasthenia. And his meridian findings indeed showed the Iron Triangle meridian pattern.

People showing this meridian pattern have usually sought medical care everywhere without ever getting better — the classic picture of autonomic dysregulation and neurasthenia.

2. Heart and Kidney failing to communicate; insufficiency of Kidney Essence

When the Heart and Kidney fail to communicate, neurasthenia can also result. This is a concept unique to Chinese medicine: according to Five Phases theory, the Heart belongs to Fire and the Kidney to Water.

Under normal circumstances Water and Fire blend, and Heart and Kidney should cooperate with each other. When the two cannot merge smoothly, the state of Heart-Kidney non-communication results.

Chinese medicine holds the view that "the Kidney stores Essence," and the TCM Kidney is closely related to the brain of modern medicine. Insufficient Kidney Essence affects the body's hormonal balance and may in turn give rise to various brain-related diseases.

One member had suffered neurasthenia for at least 10 years. Observing his meridians from 2020 onward, he found his meridian data to be remarkably stable. Why? Because he could regularly see the phenomenon of Heart meridian Excess with Deficiency of the Spleen and Kidney meridians.

The meridian pattern commonly seen in men with chronic neurasthenia.

He said his everyday symptoms matched the symptoms of neurasthenia 99%. Evidently the TCM concepts of Heart-Kidney non-communication and Kidney Essence insufficiency may truly cause neurasthenia — and observing the meridians can corroborate this phenomenon.

Large volumes of meridian data from modern people show that Deficiency of the Spleen and Kidney meridians is the norm; on this basis, modern people have a very high probability of developing neurasthenia.

Traditional Chinese medicine also holds that people with "Kidney Yin Deficiency transforming into Fire" may develop neurasthenia. In the extreme Iron Triangle meridian pattern mentioned above, a certain proportion of people show Kidney meridian Excess — perhaps this can serve to explain what Kidney Yin Deficiency transforming into Fire means.

3. Deficiency above, Excess below; Conception and Governing Vessels blocked

There are many more types of neurasthenia meridian patterns. Since the pandemic, the most common type has been "Deficiency above, Excess below." The hallmark of this meridian pattern is that the Qi and Blood of the meridians of the entire chest and abdomen are obstructed.

Viewed from the meridian perspective, one could also say the Conception Vessel (Ren Mai) and Governing Vessel (Du Mai) are blocked, so that above and below cannot communicate — hence neurasthenia may also arise.

People with Deficiency above/Excess below or Excess above/Deficiency below readily have blockage of the Conception and Governing Vessels.

4. Excess above, Deficiency below; deep-seated Cold

Since the composite meridian pattern is the most common meridian pattern, a certain proportion of neurasthenia cases likewise arise from this "Iron Triangle" plus "Yang Deficiency" meridian pattern.

In this pattern the energies of the Gallbladder, Stomach, and Bladder meridians are all very weak, resulting in insufficient Qi and Blood reaching the head — hence cerebral neurasthenia appears readily. In severe cases it becomes "Excess above, Deficiency below," causing blockage of the Conception and Governing Vessels.

Since neurasthenia is caused by overuse of the brain, the best treatment is not to use the brain — to empty the mind regularly. Meridian and acupoint patting (tapping therapy) is an excellent method of improvement.

Whatever the meridian pattern, once you know your own abnormal meridians, regularly applying meridian patting or massage to unblock these abnormal meridians can relieve cerebral neurasthenia.

Combining this with meditation and yogic breathing methods is the most fundamental way to improve neurasthenia. The renowned physician Dr. Chen Mu-chun has long taught patients his inner-core breathing method to treat insomnia without dependence on sleeping pills.

The principle of using Chinese herbs to improve neurasthenia is mainly to regulate the body's Spleen-Stomach system and keep the so-called "brain-gut axis" unobstructed (open to read); this naturally also improves neurasthenia — showing that the TCM Spleen and Stomach are intimately connected with the brain.

The human brain is a mysterious organ — and in fact a remarkably durable one! The nerve cells of the cerebral cortex are like tireless tumbler dolls able to work overtime continuously: given sufficient sleep and rest, they can quickly recover their vitality and throw themselves back into the fight.

However, under the enormous pressures of modern society, neurasthenia has become an invisible enemy for many people. When the brain's nerves are overused for long periods — like running a marathon that never stops — a moment will eventually come when the limit of endurance is exceeded.

Modern people suffer information anxiety and generally overuse their brains.

When a person suffers neurasthenia, life seems as though placed under a strange curse. Forgetting things becomes commonplace, like a goldfish with only short-term memory.

They are listless all day, as if all motivation for living has been drained away. Nothing they do can rouse their interest, and ultimately they only want to find a quiet corner to sit or lie down.

Reactions slow, and they grow indifferent to the people and things around them, which may lead others to mistake it for depression. Emotional swings are large: a small matter may plunge them into deep gloom, or anger may suddenly erupt.

Sleep is no longer easy: they are often startled awake by the slightest sound, then toss and turn, unable to fall asleep again.

This state is often classified as "psychoneurosis," "autonomic nervous system dysregulation (dysautonomia)," or "psychosomatic disorder." But on examination at the hospital, one often receives an answer that leaves one not knowing whether to laugh or cry — "There is nothing wrong with you!" — which makes the person feel even more helpless.

At this point, Chinese medicine offers another perspective for viewing and treating neurasthenia — an entirely new line of thinking!

data/pathology/condition_canon_shortlist.branch_value: Classical Chinese medicine had no term equivalent to "psoriasis" but recorded the same presentation as 白疕 (bai bi) — thick white scaling skin with itch. Sources such as Zhubing Yuanhou Lun describe dry, itchy skin resembling measles-scale that becomes progressively drier, cracked and painful with bleeding. The traditional attribution is blood deficiency generating internal wind and dryness, so the skin lacks nourishment; onset is triggered by external cold or damp-heat pathogens obstructing the collaterals at the skin surface, and with prolonged illness the cold transforms to heat and dampness to dryness, further damaging blood and worsening dryness — hence the difficulty of treatment. Recognized patterns include blood-heat, blood-dryness, blood-stasis, damp-heat and external wind-cold, with no single fixed formula given the individual variation. The source record's meridian-measurement observations associate psoriasis with weak spleen and bladder channels and the same "iron-triangle" pattern (liver excess, spleen/bladder deficiency) seen across other immune-related conditions in this dataset, worsening in winter (reduced sweating, dry indoor air, upper-respiratory infection season) and improving in summer.
data/pathology/condition_canon_shortlist.main_value:
Ancient Chinese medicine had no term 'niupixuan (psoriasis),' but that does not mean the disease did not exist in antiquity. In ancient times it was called 'bai bi' — a stubborn skin disease in which thick white scales arise on the skin, accompanied by itching.

Ancient medical texts such as the Zhubing Yuanhou Lun (Treatise on the Origins and Manifestations of Diseases) and the Yizong Jinjian (Golden Mirror of Medicine) all discussed it; for example, the Waike Zhengzhi Quanshu (Complete Book of Patterns and Treatments in External Medicine) records: 'The skin is dry and itchy, erupting like papules or scabies but white in color; scratching raises scales; gradually the limbs and body become withered and dry, cracking and splitting, with bleeding and pain.'

Traditional Chinese medicine holds that this disease arises mainly from 'Blood Deficiency' giving rise to phenomena of 'Wind' and 'Dryness' in the body, so that the skin, failing to receive adequate nourishment, becomes diseased.

At its outset the condition results from external Cold, or Damp-Heat pathogenic Qi, invading the skin, causing the flow of Qi and Blood in the channels to become inhibited and blocked at the skin surface, producing the lesions.

Chinese medicine holds that psoriasis is initially caused by Cold or Damp-Heat invading the body

If the illness drags on, the original factors of Cold, Fire-Heat, and Damp-Heat transform — the Cold pathogen turns to Heat, the Damp pathogen turns to Dryness — thereby aggravating the condition.

Finally, with Qi and Blood damaged on top of this, the Blood becomes even more insufficient and the skin even drier, and the skin's condition deteriorates further — which is why psoriasis is so hard to treat.

Traditional Chinese pattern identification proposes the possibilities of 'Blood Heat,' 'Blood Dryness,' 'Blood stasis,' 'Damp-Heat,' 'external contraction of Wind-Cold,' and other patterns.

Because of this complexity, each person's situation is different, so there is also no single fixed herbal formula that can directly treat psoriasis.

Many people still cannot make sense of the Chinese medical descriptions above, because what Chinese medicine describes is simply too abstract.

To understand what actually causes the disease of psoriasis, the simplest method is to perform meridian testing directly on psoriasis patients and observe what meridian phenomena appear, thereby cracking the underlying cause.

A certain Cloud TCM member shared her observations on skin diseases several years ago; she had studied Chinese medicine in mainland China and particularly loved researching skin diseases.

She recalled that during a period some years ago she would often go out to test patients' meridians, and she found that these psoriasis patients had a high probability of showing Deficiency in two channels — the Spleen channel and the Bladder channel — which made her very curious!

Psoriasis is closely related to the 'Iron Triangle' meridian pattern

Later, from some members' long-term observation reports, it was found that with fairly high probability, psoriasis patients present the so-called 'Iron Triangle' meridian pattern — well worth research by modern medicine.

Here is a classic case. During October 2023 a member shared his friend's psoriasis case: the friend had psoriasis on the first and third toes, the ankle, the lateral aspect of the lower limb (the Gallbladder channel pathway), and the elbows, and this had persisted for many years, troubling him greatly.

The meridian pattern of a man with psoriasis

This member was astonished to find that the locations of the psoriasis on his friend's body indeed all lay on those abnormal channels — especially the severely Excess Gallbladder channel: the psoriasis along the Gallbladder channel pathway on his thigh was particularly severe.

At other locations such as the Liver and Spleen channels, psoriasis indeed also appeared on the big toe. Obvious psoriasis also appeared at the elbows, which can be said to correspond to the Liver channel (Large Intestine channel).

In fact this meridian pattern frequently shows Excess of the Triple Burner and Large Intestine channels; although no abnormality appeared on this particular chart, one may assume it could appear at any time.

Although this chart showed his Stomach channel as normal, the psoriasis at the location of the Stomach channel's Jiexi point (ST41) was especially severe. On later occasions when the member tested him again several times, the Stomach channel did indeed more often show Excess.

Since this meridian pattern appears in most people during spring and summer, and in some people does not disappear even in autumn and winter, it happens to match modern medicine's observation: onset in spring, aggravation in winter, remission in summer.

As for why it worsens in winter, the following reasons are possible:

Reduced sweating in winter: the cold, dry weather of winter reduces psoriasis patients' sweating, which makes the pores more easily blocked, so that some harmful substances cannot be promptly and effectively cleared.

Dry winter skin: in winter, windows are opened for ventilation less often, so indoor air cannot stay circulating and becomes excessively dry.

Lowered immunity: winter is also the peak season for upper respiratory tract infections, and such infections may likewise trigger aggravation of psoriasis.

Some members have indeed had psoriasis flare in winter yet without showing the Iron Triangle meridian pattern, instead showing 'Deficiency of the three Yang channels of the hand' — the typical presentation of abdominal Cold-Damp with Yang Deficiency (see figure below).

A woman whose psoriasis flared in winter, presenting Deficiency of the three hand-Yang channels

From her meridian phenomena one can also see severe Excess of the Gallbladder channel; there seems to be a certain degree of association between the Gallbladder channel and psoriasis.

Overall, psoriasis still most often shows the Iron Triangle meridian pattern, and many members observing other immune-system diseases have found that they likewise present the Iron Triangle pattern.

In particular, people with this disease often feel inferior because of their abnormal skin and are usually in low spirits, and this emotional gloom further consolidates the Iron Triangle meridian pattern.

Clearly, people with an Iron Triangle meridian constitution who do not attend to health cultivation easily develop immune-system-related diseases (for example: diabetes, inflammatory bowel disease, scleroderma, rheumatoid arthritis, lupus erythematosus, and so on).

Even more arthritis patients likewise present the Iron Triangle meridian pattern — which suffices to explain why psoriasis patients so easily develop arthritis.

Ancient Chinese texts often made this point as well; for example, the Youyou Jicheng (Complete Compendium on Childhood Diseases) states: 'Hidden rashes mostly belong to the Spleen, for they lie hidden within the skin, and when they erupt they itch greatly' — the ancients often treated children's skin diseases from the Spleen.

Prevent and improve skin disease in summer, and it will not flare in winter

Strictly speaking, then, psoriasis counts as a 'summer disease' that flares in 'winter,' so if one cultivates health well in summer and prevents disease, it will not flare in winter.

According to the observations of many members, various skin diseases do indeed appear easily in summer. The Huangdi Neijing says: 'Wind is the chief of the hundred diseases' — this is genuinely true.

For early-stage skin disease, 'Mahuang Guizhi Gebantang (Ephedra and Cinnamon Twig Half-and-Half Decoction)' can cut it off right at the very start when the skin disease first emerges, so that the various diseases of the future will not develop from it.

For psoriasis caused by a long-term chronic constitution, some members report that using 'Yang Gan Wan (Liver-Nourishing Pill),' or 'Jiawei Xiaoyao San (Augmented Free Wanderer Powder)' plus 'Yinqiao San (Honeysuckle and Forsythia Powder),' gives quite good improvement.

Psoriasis is an immune disease, and the reason each person's immune system is damaged is different. Whatever the cause, as long as one improves one's own constitution, immunity returns to its normal state, and the related diseases all naturally improve.

data/pathology/condition_canon_shortlist.main_value:
Psoriasis is a chronic skin disease of immune-system imbalance, also known in Chinese as 'niupixuan (cattle-hide lichen)' or 'silver-scale disease.'

Its main feature is the appearance of patches of abnormal skin on the body; these patches usually show erythema, itching, and scaling. It is not a contagious disease.

Because of the immune-system imbalance, psoriasis patients have a higher likelihood of concurrently developing arthritis, lymphoma, cardiovascular disease, Crohn's disease, and depression.

Modern medicine has found that psoriasis is markedly seasonal: patients often experience onset in spring, aggravation in winter, and remission in summer, so the probability of occurrence in cold high-latitude regions is higher than in low-latitude regions.

To this day psoriasis cannot be completely cured; medications can only control the symptoms — for example corticosteroid ointments, cholecalciferol (vitamin D analogue) ointments, and so on — and some treatment drugs are extremely expensive.

Therefore, if an alternative option exists, those troubled by this disease will surely strive to pursue it, and the related treatment theories of Chinese medicine may also be considered.

data/pathology/condition_canon_shortlist.main_value:
There was no term 'herpes zoster' in antiquity, but there were quite a few similar diseases — clearly herpes zoster existed in ancient times.

Chinese medicine has no such term as immunity — only the so-called 'upright Qi (zheng qi).' When the body's Zang-Fu organs and meridians are out of balance, immunity begins to decline, and herpes zoster appears under such conditions.

Traditional Chinese medicine holds that herpes zoster is caused by external contraction of toxic pathogens producing blazing Liver Fire and Gallbladder Fire, which obstruct the channels and congeal in the skin.

1. Herpes zoster formed by Fire-Heat

From the meridian data of modern people it is found that the great majority show long-term Liver-channel Excess and Gallbladder-channel Deficiency; remaining long in this state leads to obstruction of meridian Qi and Blood, with pain along the Liver and Gallbladder channels — this is a common cause of herpes zoster.

Modern people commonly show Liver-channel Excess and Gallbladder-channel Deficiency — long-term imbalance of an exterior-interior channel pair

According to the observations of some Cloud TCM members, whenever the body is extremely fatigued, the Iron Triangle meridian pattern (Liver-channel Excess with Spleen- and Bladder-channel Deficiency) readily appears; it can thus also be called the meridian pattern of immunity beginning to decline.

At such times the pattern Chinese medicine calls 'Liver Fire flaming upward' readily appears, with frequent bitter taste in the mouth, dry mouth, agitation and irritability, dry stools, or dark-yellow urine.

This phenomenon also overlaps with what Chinese medicine calls 'Shaoyang disease,' so it produces abnormalities of the Liver, Gallbladder, and Triple Burner channels — usually caused by constrained Heat in the Liver channel.

In terms of the 'cold-heat index,' simply remaining continuously in a state of 'heat both above and below' creates the opportunity for herpes zoster to appear.

People with the 'Iron Triangle meridian constitution' show the Iron Triangle pattern long-term with simultaneous Excess of the Shaoyang channels (Triple Burner, Gallbladder) and the Yangming channels (Large Intestine, Stomach); when at a certain point in time Heat forms internally, herpes zoster appears.

The Iron Triangle meridian pattern appears with fatigue or hot-humid weather

In particular, modern people's long-term Triple Burner-channel Excess indicates exuberant internal Fire. This suffices to explain why some people's herpes zoster appears near the ears — a phenomenon of 'blazing toxic Heat' within the body. Hence herpes zoster readily appears in summer.

This internal constrained Heat may also come from long-term dietary indulgence: Damp-Heat brews in the body over time, producing severe Spleen Deficiency with Damp-Heat; Dampness obstructs the Qi dynamic and accumulates stagnantly in the skin, producing skin herpes and vesicles.

Since the Iron Triangle meridian pattern is closely related to emotions, if a person's emotions suddenly collapse (death of family or friends, unemployment, divorce, bankruptcy, and so on) or stress becomes excessive, the Iron Triangle pattern may also appear, and with it herpes zoster.

Not only for herpes zoster — in treating many skin diseases Chinese medicine can start from removing internal Damp-Heat. Everyone may look at the Spleen channel's pathway: it also passes through the chest and intercostal region, which are likewise common sites of herpes zoster.

2. Herpes zoster formed by Yin Cold

Traditional Chinese treatment of herpes zoster proceeds mainly from Liver-Gallbladder Fire-Heat and Spleen-Stomach Damp-Heat brewing toxin — but can the Cold pathogen not produce herpes zoster?

Modern medicine finds that herpes zoster readily appears in winter and early spring — especially in spring, when the weather swings abruptly between cold and hot, and the resulting lowered immunity also favors the appearance of herpes zoster.

Yet the meridian patterns common in winter are in fact the complete opposite of those during summer; clearly, both 'excessive Cold' and 'excessive Heat' within the body lower immunity and trigger herpes zoster.

After entering autumn and winter, meridian disorder causes immunity to decline

Taking autumn as an example: as the temperature falls, the energies of the Gallbladder, Stomach, and Kidney channels of the original summer Iron Triangle also begin to decline, and at this time the body's immunity drops rapidly.

Taking spring as an example: it very easily continues the 'Yang Deficiency' meridian pattern common in winter. Take April 2023: although it was already late spring about to enter summer, a cold front still appeared in Taiwan, and it felt exactly like winter.

One member reported that his herpes zoster had recurred, and his physical-energy index was only 17. Such a low energy index usually indicates poor circulation of Qi and Blood within the body; all the channels of his lower body were Deficient, driving Excess of the upper-body channels (see figure below).

A case of herpes zoster appearing as the weather temperature dropped

In particular, the Fire-Heat of the Triple Burner channel was severe — this is in fact rooted in the insufficiency of lower-body channel energy brought on by the cold weather, presenting the 'Excess above, Deficiency below' meridian phenomenon.

This 'Excess above, Deficiency below' meridian pattern very easily appears in the middle-aged and elderly; this member was about 60 years old, matching that age. Modern medicine finds that the elderly readily develop herpes zoster, and the meridian model behind it should be this meridian phenomenon.

In terms of the 'cold-heat index,' remaining long-term in a state of 'heat above, cold below' or 'cold both above and below' creates the opportunity for herpes zoster to appear.

In sum, if a person's body long remains excessively Fire-Hot, or excessively Yin-Cold, immunity declines, thereby inducing activation of the herpes virus and the appearance of herpes zoster.

If this meridian constitution is not improved, more diseases will develop later on, and true recovery will not occur — so improving the meridian constitution is the most fundamental method.

As of 2023, the data show that the 'Iron Triangle meridian constitution' most readily triggers herpes zoster, followed by the 'Excess above, Deficiency below' meridian pattern.

Summer or emotional stress most readily drives the 'Iron Triangle meridian pattern' toward severity, and winter most readily drives the 'Excess above, Deficiency below' pattern toward severity; these, then, are the meridian models by which these two seasons induce herpes zoster.

data/pathology/condition_canon_shortlist.branch_value: Condensed translation: the essay describes shingles as reactivation of latent varicella-zoster virus in roughly 1 in 3 people over a lifetime, triggered by age, illness or lowered immunity, producing painful vesicular dermatomal rash typically resolving in 2-4 weeks — an entry point for the TCM etiologies described in etiology_zh, not itself a full biomedical VZV mechanism.
data/pathology/condition_canon_shortlist.main_value:
Herpes zoster (shingles) is a common disease; taking Taiwan as an example, one in every three people may suffer at least one episode of herpes zoster in their lifetime.

Herpes zoster can occur at any age, because after each person recovers from varicella-zoster virus infection, the virus does not thereupon disappear; it remains latent for life within the body's nerve ganglia.

These viruses can be reactivated with advancing age, illness, or lowered immunity — the probability is higher in the elderly — causing bodily pain and the appearance of red rashes and blisters on the skin surface.

It is thus like a time bomb inside the human body: once immunity begins to decline, the virus is readily activated and proliferates, triggering herpes zoster.

The elderly, and immunocompromised groups with chronic diseases (diabetes, kidney disease, asthma, cancer, and so on), have 1.24 to 9 times the general population's probability of developing herpes zoster.

Diseases in which herpes viruses are activated by lowered immunity are not limited to this one; in recent years research has found that 'depression' may also form in this way.

At onset, herpes zoster produces skin pain, prickling itch, aching numbness, and burning sensations; erythema and vesicles emerge on the skin, usually healing within 2-4 weeks.

The most common locations are the chest and neck, around the eyes and ears, and the facial distribution area of the trigeminal nerve; it also appears on the back and around the waist.

Under fatigue and lowered immunity, the herpes zoster virus begins to reactivate

Since this is a disease that manifests lowered immunity, the treatment methods are only to ease and relieve the sensation of pain — topical anesthetic patches, low-level laser, or nerve block; most of the time no treatment is needed, and it heals by itself within days to weeks!

In 2023 a member shared that he had previously contracted herpes zoster abroad; at the time the Western doctor did not prescribe him a single pill, only asking him to rest and sleep at home. He then slept all day, and after a week he had recovered.

Diseases like this, arising from lowered internal immunity, are the most suitable for applying Chinese medical theory; as long as the meridians' Qi and Blood are balanced, healing can be accelerated.

data/pathology/tdis_registry.json.branch_value: 吞酸是以酸水上泛，甚則酸水刺喉、口中泛酸為主要表現的病證，多因肝胃不和、胃失和降，或脾胃虛寒、濕濁上泛所致。
data/pathology/tdis_registry.json.main_value: 吞酸指胃中酸水上泛、逆流入食道之病證。本講義以西醫胃食道逆流病（GERD）立論：因下食道括約肌（LES）功能不全，胃酸持續逆流入食道，刺激損傷黏膜，臨床以胃灼熱與泛酸為主症，為最常見之食道疾病。

data/pathology/tdis_registry.json.branch_value: Tun Suan (Acid Regurgitation) is characterized by acid fluid rising up, with severe cases irritating the throat and a sour taste in the mouth, usually due to Liver-Stomach disharmony with Stomach failing to descend, or Spleen-Stomach Cold-deficiency with turbid Dampness rising.
data/pathology/tdis_registry.json.main_value: Tun suan (acid regurgitation) denotes sour gastric fluid surging upward into the esophagus. The handout presents it as gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD): a chronic condition in which gastric acid flows back into the esophagus due to lower esophageal sphincter (LES) incompetence, irritating and damaging the mucosa; heartburn and regurgitation are the cardinal symptoms, and it is the most common esophageal disease.

data/pathology/tdis_registry.json.branch_value: 情志不遂，肝氣犯胃，肝胃鬱熱；或飲食不節，脾胃損傷，寒濕內生，濁氣上逆。
data/pathology/tdis_registry.json.main_value: 講義所列危險因子：肥胖（腹內壓增高）、食道裂孔疝（胃酸更易逆流）、懷孕（激素與機械性壓迫）、抽菸與飲酒（鬆弛下食道括約肌）、嗜食辛辣油膩（誘發逆流）。中醫方面，講義指出肝胃不和型之逆流多由情志緊張（壓力）誘發。

data/pathology/tdis_registry.json.branch_value: Emotional frustration causes Liver Qi to invade the Stomach, producing Liver-Stomach depressive Heat; or dietary irregularity injures the Spleen-Stomach, generating internal Cold-Damp with turbid Qi rebelling upward.
data/pathology/tdis_registry.json.main_value: Risk factors listed in the handout: obesity (raised intra-abdominal pressure), hiatal hernia (allows acid to reflux more easily), pregnancy (hormonal and mechanical pressure), smoking and alcohol (both relax the LES), and spicy or fatty food (triggers reflux). On the TCM side, the handout notes that reflux of the Liver-invading-Stomach type is triggered by emotional stress.

data/pathology/tdis_registry.json.branch_value: 肝鬱化熱，橫逆犯胃，胃失和降，胃氣挾酸上逆則吞酸嘈雜；脾胃虛寒者運化失司，濕濁內停，隨胃氣上泛則泛吐清水酸水。
data/pathology/tdis_registry.json.main_value: 下食道括約肌鬆弛，胃酸逆流入食道，致黏膜刺激與糜爛；久病可發展為Barrett食道（腸化生），進而增加腺癌風險。中醫整合部分分三型：肝胃不和、胃熱上逆、脾胃虛寒，皆以酸水上逆為共同病機表現。

data/pathology/tdis_registry.json.branch_value: Liver depression transforms into Heat and invades the Stomach transversely; the Stomach loses its harmonious descent, and Stomach Qi carrying acid rebels upward, producing acid regurgitation and gnawing hunger sensation. In Spleen-Stomach Cold-deficiency, transportation fails, internal Damp-turbidity accumulates, and rises with Stomach Qi to produce watery, sour regurgitation.
data/pathology/tdis_registry.json.main_value: LES incompetence permits acid reflux into the esophagus, causing mucosal irritation and erosion; if chronic, Barrett esophagus (intestinal metaplasia) may develop, raising the risk of adenocarcinoma. The TCM integration section differentiates three types — Liver invading Stomach, Stomach heat rebelling upward, and Spleen-Stomach deficiency cold — all sharing upward counterflow of acid as the common mechanism.

key_manifestations_zh: 泛酸，或嘈雜似饑
胸骨後或胃脘部灼熱感
噯氣、噁心
夜臥或飽食後加重
可伴胸悶脅痛
key_manifestations_en: Acid regurgitation, or gnawing hunger-like sensation
Retrosternal or epigastric burning sensation
Belching and nausea
Worsens lying down at night or after a full meal
May accompany chest oppression and rib-side pain

key_manifestations_zh: 胃灼熱，餐後、平臥、彎腰時加重
泛酸／胃酸逆流，口中有酸苦味
吞嚥困難（警訊症狀，須排除食道狹窄或惡性病變）
胸痛（須先排除心源性病因）
慢性咳嗽、聲音沙啞（食道外／非典型表現）
key_manifestations_en: Heartburn, worse after meals, when lying flat, or bending over
Regurgitation of gastric acid with a sour or bitter taste in the mouth
Dysphagia (alarm symptom; rule out stricture or malignancy)
Chest pain (cardiac cause must be ruled out first)
Chronic cough and hoarseness (extra-esophageal / atypical presentation)

課件另載證型(詞彙表無 id,未強配): 胃熱上逆、脾胃虛寒。

data/pathology/tdis_registry.json.branch_value: 呃逆是以氣逆上衝，喉間呃呃連聲，聲短而頻，不能自止為主要表現的病證，多因胃氣上逆動膈所致。
data/pathology/tdis_registry.json.main_value: 呃逆係指膈肌不自主收縮,呃聲頻頻,一分鐘內可反覆多次發作,不能自制的病證。

data/pathology/tdis_registry.json.branch_value: E Ni (Hiccup) is characterized by Qi rebelling upward with short, frequent hiccupping sounds in the throat that cannot be controlled, usually due to Stomach Qi rebelling upward and disturbing the diaphragm.
data/pathology/tdis_registry.json.main_value: Hiccup refers to an involuntary contraction of the diaphragm that may repeat several times per minute.

data/pathology/tdis_registry.json.branch_value: 飲食不節（過食生冷、辛熱）、情志不遂、正氣虧虛、久病體弱，皆可致胃失和降，氣逆動膈。
data/pathology/tdis_registry.json.main_value: 西醫病因:進食過速,碳酸飲料與酒,某些藥物。中醫病因分虛實:實者為胃中寒冷、胃火上逆、氣鬱痰阻(每因情志緊張、焦慮而誘發);虛者為胃陽不足、胃陰虧虛。

data/pathology/tdis_registry.json.branch_value: Dietary irregularity (excess raw-cold or spicy-hot food), emotional frustration, upright Qi deficiency, or chronic debility can all cause the Stomach to lose its harmonious descent, with Qi rebelling to disturb the diaphragm.
data/pathology/tdis_registry.json.main_value: Western causes given in the handout: rapid eating; carbonated beverages and alcohol; certain drugs. In Chinese medicine the causes divide into excess conditions — stomach cold, stomach fire, and qi-phlegm stagnation (induced by stress or anxiety) — and deficiency conditions — stomach yang deficiency and stomach yin deficiency.

key_manifestations_zh: 喉間呃呃連聲，聲短而頻
不能自主控制
可因飲食、情緒或受寒誘發
輕者偶發自止，重者晝夜不停
key_manifestations_en: Short, frequent hiccupping sounds in the throat
Cannot be voluntarily controlled
May be triggered by diet, emotion, or cold exposure
Mild cases self-resolve; severe cases persist day and night

key_manifestations_zh: 呃聲頻作,不能自制,一分鐘內可反覆多次
胃寒者呃聲深長有力,胃脘冷痛;胃火者呃聲洪亮清晰有力,口舌生瘡
氣鬱痰阻者呃逆連連不止,兼嘔吐,遇情志緊張焦慮而發
胃陽虛者呃聲低弱沉緩,肢冷倦怠,納差;胃陰虛者呃聲短促急速,口乾唇燥而渴
key_manifestations_en: Repeated involuntary hiccups that may recur several times per minute
In stomach cold the sound is deep, long and forceful with cramping stomach pain; in stomach fire it is loud, clear and forceful with mouth ulcers
In qi-phlegm stagnation the hiccups are continuous with vomiting, induced by stress or anxiety
In stomach yang deficiency the sound is weak, deep and low-toned with cold limbs, fatigue and poor appetite; in stomach yin deficiency it is short and quick with thirst and dry mouth, tongue and lips

課件另載證型(詞彙表無 id,未強配): 胃中寒冷、氣鬱痰阻、胃陽虛。

data/pathology/tdis_registry.json.branch_value: 泄瀉是以大便次數增多、糞質稀溏甚則如水樣為主症的病證，古人以大便溏薄勢緩者為泄、暴注下迫者為瀉，現多合稱。
data/pathology/tdis_registry.json.main_value: 泄瀉係指排便次數增多,每日三次或以上,糞質稀溏或呈水樣的病證;其病與脾、肝、腎三臟關係最為密切。

data/pathology/tdis_registry.json.branch_value: Xie Xie (Diarrhea) is a disease characterized by increased stool frequency with loose or watery stools. Classically, gradual loose stools were called Xie and sudden forceful watery discharge was called Xie (瀉); the two are now usually combined under one name.
data/pathology/tdis_registry.json.main_value: Diarrhea refers to the condition of having three or more loose or liquid bowel movements per day; the zangfu chiefly involved are the spleen, liver, and kidney.

data/pathology/tdis_registry.json.branch_value: 多因感受外邪（寒濕、濕熱）、飲食不節或不潔、情志失調（肝氣乘脾），或脾胃虛弱、命門火衰（腎陽虛）所致。
data/pathology/tdis_registry.json.main_value: 感受外邪(風、暑、濕、寒、熱);飲食所傷(暴飲暴食);情志失調(郁怒致肝氣鬱結,橫逆乘脾);脾胃虛弱;腎陽虧虛。

data/pathology/tdis_registry.json.branch_value: Commonly caused by external pathogens (Cold-Damp or Damp-Heat), dietary irregularity or contaminated food, emotional disturbance (Liver Qi overacting on the Spleen), or an underlying Spleen-Stomach weakness or Kidney Yang (Gate of Vitality Fire) deficiency.
data/pathology/tdis_registry.json.main_value: Affection by external pathogens (wind, summerheat, damp, cold, and heat); dietary injury (overeating); emotional disturbance (anger leading to liver qi stagnation overacting on the spleen); spleen and stomach weakness; kidney yang deficiency.

data/pathology/tdis_registry.json.branch_value: 脾主運化、喜燥惡濕；濕邪困脾、食滯腸胃或肝木乘土，皆令脾失健運、水穀不化、清濁不分而下趨大腸作瀉；久瀉傷及脾腎陽氣，則轉為虛寒久瀉。
data/pathology/tdis_registry.json.main_value: 外邪侵襲(寒濕、濕熱)或飲食積滯,損傷脾胃,運化失司,發為急性泄瀉,多屬實證;病久不癒,則見肝氣橫逆乘脾、脾胃虛弱不能運化水穀、或腎陽虧虛不能溫煦,轉為慢性泄瀉,多屬虛證;腎陽虛者每於黎明之前腸鳴腹痛而瀉,瀉後始安。病位雖在腸,而關鍵繫於脾,並涉及肝腎。

data/pathology/tdis_registry.json.branch_value: The Spleen governs transportation and transformation and prefers dryness over dampness. Whether Dampness encumbers the Spleen, food stagnates in the intestines, or the Liver (Wood) overacts on the Spleen (Earth), the Spleen loses its transporting function, food and fluids go untransformed, clear and turbid fail to separate, and the mixture pours down into the large intestine as diarrhea. Chronic diarrhea injures Spleen-Kidney Yang, shifting the pattern to a chronic Cold-vacuity type.
data/pathology/tdis_registry.json.main_value: Invasion by external pathogens (cold-damp, damp-heat) or food stagnation injures the spleen and stomach, whose transportation and transformation fail, producing acute diarrhea, mostly of excess type. When prolonged, liver qi overacting on the spleen, spleen-stomach weakness unable to transform food, or kidney yang deficiency failing to warm gives rise to chronic diarrhea, mostly of deficient type; in kidney yang deficiency the diarrhea occurs before dawn, preceded by borborygmus and abdominal pain and eased after the bowel movement. The disease is located in the intestines, with the spleen as the pivot, and also involves the liver and kidney.

key_manifestations_zh: 大便次數增多、質稀或如水樣
腹痛腸鳴
可伴脘腹脹悶、食慾不振
情緒緊張時發作或加重（肝鬱乘脾者）
久瀉者黎明前腹瀉（五更瀉，腎陽虛）
key_manifestations_en: Increased stool frequency, loose or watery
Abdominal pain with borborygmus
May accompany epigastric fullness and poor appetite
Triggered or worsened by emotional stress (Liver-Spleen disharmony)
Pre-dawn diarrhea in chronic cases ("fifth-watch diarrhea," Kidney Yang deficiency)

key_manifestations_zh: 排便次數明顯增多,每日三次或以上
糞質稀溏,色黃,氣味酸臭,或夾黏液及未消化食物
腹痛
腸鳴
肛門墜重、灼熱
key_manifestations_en: Markedly increased bowel movement frequency, three or more times per day
Loose stool, yellow in color, with a sour odor, mucus, or undigested food
Abdominal pain
Borborygmus
Heavy sensation and burning of the anus

data/pathology/tdis_registry.json.branch_value: 便秘是以大便秘結不通、排便間隔延長，或糞質乾硬、排出艱難為主症的病證。
data/pathology/tdis_registry.json.main_value: 便秘係指排便困難、便後有排便不盡感,且排便次數減少(一般每週三次或以下)的病證。

data/pathology/tdis_registry.json.branch_value: Bian Mi (Constipation) is a disease characterized by infrequent, difficult, or incomplete bowel movements with hard, dry stool.
data/pathology/tdis_registry.json.main_value: Constipation refers to a condition of difficulty during defecation, a sensation of incomplete bowel evacuation, and infrequent bowel movements, typically three times or fewer per week.

data/pathology/tdis_registry.json.branch_value: 多因飲食不節（辛熱厚味、飲水過少）、情志不遂（肝鬱氣滯）、年老體虛（氣血陰陽不足）或久坐少動所致。
data/pathology/tdis_registry.json.main_value: 講義所列病因:飲食失宜(膳食纖維與水分攝取不足,嗜食辛辣、乾燥、高蛋白、高脂之品)、藥物所傷、焦慮等情志因素、戒菸、腹部手術、肛門括約肌損傷、腫瘤梗阻、乳糖不耐等。中醫辨其虛實:實者為腸胃積熱與氣機鬱滯;虛者為血虛、陰虛、氣虛、陽虛。

data/pathology/tdis_registry.json.branch_value: Commonly caused by dietary factors (excessive spicy/rich food, insufficient fluid intake), emotional disturbance (Liver Qi stagnation), advancing age with underlying vacuity (Qi, Blood, Yin, or Yang deficiency), or a sedentary lifestyle.
data/pathology/tdis_registry.json.main_value: Causes listed in the handout: dietary factors (insufficient fiber and water intake; spicy-pungent, dry, high-protein and high-fat foods), medications, anxiety and other psychological factors, smoking cessation, abdominal surgery, damage to the anal sphincter, tumor obstruction, and lactose intolerance. In TCM it is differentiated into excess conditions (gastrointestinal heat and qi stagnation) and deficient conditions (blood deficiency, yin deficiency, qi deficiency, yang deficiency).

data/pathology/tdis_registry.json.branch_value: 大腸主傳導，以通為用；燥熱內結、氣機鬱滯，皆令大腸傳導失司、糟粕內停而秘結；氣血陰陽虧虛者，則腸道失於濡潤或推動無力，亦致大便艱澀。
data/pathology/tdis_registry.json.main_value: 其病機不外排便受阻與腸道傳導遲緩兩端。實者腸胃積熱,津液受灼,或氣機鬱滯,腑氣不通,故大便乾結、排出困難,情志波動則加重;虛者血虛陰虛,腸道失於濡潤,大便乾燥難下,或氣虛陽虛,大腸傳送無力、蠕動遲緩,雖糞便蓄積而便意不生,或雖有便意而努掙難出,便後短氣汗出、疲乏,甚者須賴瀉藥方得一行。

data/pathology/tdis_registry.json.branch_value: The large intestine governs conveyance and functions best when unobstructed. Internal Dryness-Heat binding or Qi stagnation both impair the large intestine's conveying function, causing waste to accumulate and stools to bind. In Qi, Blood, Yin, or Yang deficiency, the intestines lack moistening or propulsive force, likewise producing difficult defecation.
data/pathology/tdis_registry.json.main_value: The mechanisms fall into two categories: obstructed defecation and hypomotility. In excess patterns, gastrointestinal heat scorches the fluids, or stagnant qi blocks the bowel qi, so the stool is dry and difficult to pass, worsening with emotional fluctuation. In deficiency patterns, blood or yin deficiency deprives the intestines of moistening so the dry stool is hard to pass, or qi and yang deficiency leaves the large intestine without propulsive force and peristalsis slows — the urge to defecate may be absent even when feces have accumulated, or defecation remains difficult and is followed by shortness of breath, sweating and fatigue, in severe cases relying on purgatives.

key_manifestations_zh: 大便秘結、排便間隔延長
糞質乾硬難下
腹脹或腹部隱痛
排便費力、便後仍覺不盡
可伴口臭、面色無華（虛證）
key_manifestations_en: Infrequent, bound bowel movements
Hard, dry stool that is difficult to pass
Abdominal distension or dull discomfort
Straining with a sense of incomplete evacuation
May accompany bad breath or a sallow complexion in vacuity patterns

key_manifestations_zh: 大便乾結,排便困難
排便次數減少,每週三次或以下
便後有排便不盡感
腹部脹滿
或需藉手法或瀉藥始能排便
key_manifestations_en: Dry, hard stool with difficulty in defecation
Infrequent bowel movements, three times or fewer per week
Sensation of incomplete bowel evacuation
Abdominal distension
May require manual maneuvers or purgatives to facilitate defecation

data/pathology/tdis_registry.json.main_value: 脅痛係指以一側或兩側脅肋部疼痛為主要表現的病證;其病與肝膽、脾胃、腎相關。

data/pathology/tdis_registry.json.branch_value: Xie Tong (Hypochondriac Pain) is characterized by pain in one or both rib-side (hypochondriac) regions; the disease location is mainly the Liver and Gallbladder, closely related to emotion and diet.
data/pathology/tdis_registry.json.main_value: Hypochondriac pain refers to a disorder characterized by pain over the unilateral or bilateral sides of the hypochondriac region; the zangfu involved are the liver and gallbladder, spleen and stomach, and kidney.

data/pathology/tdis_registry.json.branch_value: 情志不遂，肝氣鬱結；飲食不節，濕熱蘊結肝膽；跌僕閃挫，瘀血停著；或久病體虛，肝陰不足，脈絡失養。
data/pathology/tdis_registry.json.main_value: 總由外邪侵襲、飲食所傷、七情內傷所致。實證:肝氣鬱結;瘀血停著(氣血運行不暢);肝膽濕熱(痰濕外侵、飲食過度)。虛證:肝陰不足;飲停脅下;少陽經受病(邪鬱少陽)。

data/pathology/tdis_registry.json.branch_value: Emotional frustration causing Liver Qi stagnation; dietary irregularity generating Damp-Heat accumulation in the Liver and Gallbladder; trauma or sprain causing Blood stasis to lodge; or chronic debility with Liver Yin insufficiency depriving the network vessels of nourishment.
data/pathology/tdis_registry.json.main_value: Caused overall by affection by exterior pathogens, dietary injury, and the seven emotional factors. Excess conditions: liver qi stagnation; blood stasis (failure of the free flow of qi and blood); damp-heat in the liver and gallbladder (phlegm-damp invasion, overeating). Deficiency conditions: liver yin deficiency; fluid retention in the hypochondrium; Shaoyang meridian disease (stagnation of pathogens).

data/pathology/tdis_registry.json.branch_value: 肝主疏泄，喜條達；肝氣鬱結，疏泄失常，氣機阻滯脅絡則脹痛；濕熱蘊結肝膽，氣血壅滯則脅痛拒按；瘀血停滯脅絡，不通則痛，痛有定處；肝陰不足，脈絡失養，則隱痛綿綿。
data/pathology/tdis_registry.json.main_value: 實者氣滯、血瘀、濕熱壅阻,肝膽氣血失於流暢,不通則痛,故起病急、病程短、痛處拒按,見於體實之人;虛者肝陰虧虛,脈絡失養,不榮則痛,故起病緩、病程長、痛處喜按,見於體弱之人。本病常虛實並見,日久每轉為陰虛與氣滯並存。

data/pathology/tdis_registry.json.branch_value: The Liver governs free coursing and favors unimpeded flow. Liver Qi stagnation disrupts this function, obstructing Qi in the rib-side network vessels and causing distending pain. Damp-Heat accumulation in the Liver-Gallbladder congests Qi and Blood, causing pain worse with pressure. Blood stasis lodging in the rib-side vessels causes fixed, unrelenting pain. Liver Yin insufficiency depriving the vessels of nourishment causes a dull, lingering ache.
data/pathology/tdis_registry.json.main_value: In excess, qi stagnation, blood stasis, or damp-heat obstruction blocks the free flow of qi and blood in the liver and gallbladder — where there is blockage there is pain — hence rapid onset, short duration, refusal of pressure, and a strong constitution. In deficiency, liver yin insufficiency leaves the vessels unnourished — where there is malnourishment there is pain — hence slow onset, long duration, preference for pressure, and a weak constitution. Hypochondriac pain often presents with both excess and deficiency, and over time evolves into coexisting yin deficiency and qi stagnation.

陰虛者痛勢隱隱，伴口乾
key_manifestations_en: Distending or stabbing pain in one or both hypochondriac regions
Fluctuates with emotional state

Yin deficiency type: dull lingering pain with dry mouth

key_manifestations_zh: 一側或兩側脅肋部疼痛,呈脹痛、刺痛、隱痛、灼痛或絞痛
疼痛可放射至肩背
疼痛每因情志波動而增減
口苦
目視昏花

Pain may radiate to the shoulder and back
Pain relieved or exacerbated by emotional fluctuations
Bitter taste in the mouth
Blurred vision

data/pathology/tdis_registry.json.branch_value: 痔瘡是以肛門直腸末端靜脈叢曲張、腫脹，或伴出血、脫出、疼痛為主要表現的肛腸病證，多因臟腑本虛、大腸氣血運行不暢，兼濕熱下注、風燥傷絡所致。
data/pathology/tdis_registry.json.main_value: 痔瘡係指直腸下端或肛門部靜脈瘀血擴張所形成之柔軟腫塊，以肛門腫痛、瘙癢、便血為主要表現的病證。生於齒線以上、肛內直腸下端者為內痔；生於齒線以下、肛門口者為外痔，可脫出肛外。其病與肝膽、脾胃、腎、肺諸臟腑相關。

data/pathology/tdis_registry.json.branch_value: Zhi Chuang (Hemorrhoids) is an anorectal disease characterized by varicose, swollen venous plexuses at the anorectal junction, with possible bleeding, prolapse, or pain, usually due to underlying organ deficiency and poor Qi-Blood flow in the Large Intestine, compounded by Damp-Heat pouring downward or Wind-Dryness injuring the vessels.
data/pathology/tdis_registry.json.main_value: Hemorrhoids are painful, swollen veins in the lower portion of the rectum or anus, presenting mainly with anal pain, itching, and bleeding. Internal hemorrhoids occur just inside the anus above the pectinate line; external hemorrhoids occur at the anal opening below the pectinate line and may hang outside the anus. The zangfu involved are the Liver and Gallbladder, Spleen and Stomach, Kidney, and Lung.

data/pathology/tdis_registry.json.branch_value: 飲食不節，嗜食辛辣厚味，濕熱內生；久坐久立、久瀉久痢或妊娠，致氣血運行不暢；素體虛弱，中氣下陷，脈絡鬆弛。
data/pathology/tdis_registry.json.main_value: 情志失調、精神緊張；飲食不節；久坐久立；長期便祕或泄瀉。

data/pathology/tdis_registry.json.branch_value: Dietary irregularity with excess spicy, rich food generating internal Damp-Heat; prolonged sitting/standing, chronic diarrhea/dysentery, or pregnancy impeding Qi-Blood flow; or constitutional weakness with Center Qi sinking and lax vessels.
data/pathology/tdis_registry.json.main_value: Mental stress; improper diet; prolonged sitting or standing; chronic constipation or diarrhea.

data/pathology/tdis_registry.json.branch_value: 濕熱下注大腸，壅滯肛門，脈絡損傷，血不循經則便血；氣血瘀滯，脈絡曲張隆起則成痔核；中氣下陷者肛門失於固攝，則痔核脫出。
data/pathology/tdis_registry.json.main_value: 講義未設專門病機論述，據其證型分類可知：濕熱下注大腸，或風邪襲擾腸絡而動血，或血行瘀滯結聚肛門，或脾虛中氣下陷、升舉無力而痔核脫出，均可發為本病。

data/pathology/tdis_registry.json.branch_value: Damp-Heat pouring down into the Large Intestine congests the anus and injures the vessels, causing Blood to leave its pathway and produce bleeding stool. Qi-Blood stagnation causes the vessels to distend and bulge into hemorrhoidal masses. Center Qi sinking leaves the anus unable to hold, causing the hemorrhoidal mass to prolapse.
data/pathology/tdis_registry.json.main_value: The handout has no dedicated pathomechanism discussion; from its pattern classification, the disease arises when damp-heat pours into the intestines, or intestinal wind disturbs the collaterals and stirs the blood, or blood stagnates and binds at the anus, or spleen deficiency with sinking qi fails to lift, causing prolapse of the hemorrhoids.

key_manifestations_zh: 便血，色鮮紅，或滴血、噴射狀出血
肛門腫物脫出，便後可自行回納或需用手托回
肛門墜脹、疼痛或瘙癢
久病氣虛者痔核脫出不能回納
key_manifestations_en: Bloody stool, bright red, dripping or spurting
Prolapsed anal mass, self-reducing or requiring manual reduction after defecation
Anal heaviness, pain, or itching
Chronic Qi-deficient cases: irreducible prolapse

key_manifestations_zh: 肛門瘙癢
肛門痠痛或疼痛
便時見鮮紅血，附於糞便、手紙或滴入便池
排便時疼痛
肛門旁一個或多個質硬觸痛之腫塊
key_manifestations_en: Anal itching
Anal ache or pain
Bright red blood on toilet tissue, stool, or in the toilet bowl
Pain during bowel movements
One or more hard, tender lumps near the anus

data/pathology/tdis_registry.json.branch_value: 眩暈是以頭暈目眩、視物旋轉或站立不穩為主要表現的病證，輕者閉目可止，重者如坐舟車，甚則暈仆。
data/pathology/tdis_registry.json.main_value: 眩暈是指頭暈與目眩並見的病證：頭暈者自覺頭腦昏沉、如將暈厥；眩者視物旋轉、如坐舟車。症狀可持續或呈發作性，歷時數分鐘至數小時，常因體位變動而誘發；病情有輕重之分，輕者為輕度眩暈，重者為重度眩暈。

data/pathology/tdis_registry.json.branch_value: Xuan Yun (Dizziness) is a disease characterized by dizziness, blurred or spinning vision, or unsteadiness. Mild cases resolve on closing the eyes; severe cases feel like being on a boat or vehicle, and the most severe may cause collapse.
data/pathology/tdis_registry.json.main_value: Dizziness and vertigo is a condition combining two different feelings: lightheadedness, a feeling of being about to faint, and vertigo, a spinning sensation. Symptoms can be constant or episodic, last from minutes to hours, and onset can be triggered by a movement; it is categorized into mild vertigo and severe vertigo.

data/pathology/tdis_registry.json.branch_value: 多因情志不遂、肝陽偏亢；或飲食不節、脾失健運、痰濕內生；或久病體虛、氣血不足；或年老腎虧、精髓不充所致。
data/pathology/tdis_registry.json.main_value: 病因分外感與內傷兩類（外因與內因）。

data/pathology/tdis_registry.json.branch_value: Commonly caused by emotional stress leading to Liver Yang hyperactivity; or an improper diet impairing Spleen transportation and generating internal Phlegm-Dampness; or chronic illness with Qi-Blood deficiency; or aging with Kidney depletion and insufficient Marrow.
data/pathology/tdis_registry.json.main_value: The causes are classified into external causes and internal causes.

data/pathology/tdis_registry.json.branch_value: 肝陽上亢、肝風內動,擾動清空;或痰濕中阻,清陽不升;或氣血虧虛,清竅失養;或腎精不足,髓海空虛,皆可發為眩暈。
data/pathology/tdis_registry.json.main_value: 其病機主要有五：肝陽上亢，上擾清竅；痰濁阻滯，清陽不升；瘀血內停，脈絡不通；氣血兩虛，清竅失養；腎精不足，髓海空虛。

data/pathology/tdis_registry.json.branch_value: Whether from Liver Yang rising and Liver Wind stirring internally to disturb the clear space of the head, Phlegm-Dampness obstructing the Middle so clear Yang fails to ascend, Qi-Blood deficiency failing to nourish the clear orifices, or Kidney Essence deficiency leaving the Sea of Marrow empty — any of these mechanisms can produce dizziness.
data/pathology/tdis_registry.json.main_value: Five main mechanisms are described: liver yang uprising, phlegm obstruction, blood stagnation, qi and blood deficiency, and kidney essence insufficiency.

站立不穩

勞累或情緒波動誘發加重
key_manifestations_en: Dizziness with blurred vision
Sensation of spinning or the room spinning

Nausea or vomiting
